fix(clone): include cidata.img in cloudimg snapshot and restore its path

Snapshot was missing the per-VM cloud-init disk (cidata.img) for cloudimg
VMs. Added cidata copy during snapshot creation and path rewrite during
clone. Moved verifyBaseFiles after cidata path update so it validates the
correct path.

fix(api): correct CH net config JSON tag and add console path logging

CH uses "net" (not "nets") as the JSON key for network devices.
The wrong tag caused parsed config to silently lose all network entries.
Added Infof log for resolved console path to aid debugging.

fix(clone): suppress CH default tap IP and fix net multi-queue calculation

Added explicit IP/Mask fields (JSON null) to chNet so CH skips its
default 192.168.249.1/24 tap configuration, which fails in managed
netns. Added netNumQueues helper to compute correct virtio queue count
(cpu*2 for multi-queue) for use in both CLI args and config.json.

feat(snapshot): capture and restore image reference in snapshot metadata

Snapshot now records the source VM's image name (e.g. "ubuntu:22.04").
Clone inherits the image reference when the user doesn't specify one.
Added Image field to SnapshotConfig and propagated through Create,
Restore, and the localfile backend.

refactor(console): replace containerd/console with moby/term

Switched terminal handling to moby/term, removing the custom EscapeProxy
and ctx-wrapped reader. Relay is now simpler: the caller's defer Close()
unblocks the remaining goroutine. HandleResize uses moby/term's
GetWinsize/SetWinsize. Fixed several lint issues (shadow, gofumpt).

fix(console): force SIGWINCH on connect via PTY size nudge

After vm.restore the remote PTY may already have matching dimensions,
making a plain SetWinsize a no-op (TIOCSWINSZ only sends SIGWINCH on
actual change). Nudge width+1 then set correct size to guarantee a
redraw.

fix(console): inject Ctrl+L for post-restore screen redraw

Replace the SIGWINCH nudge with a simpler Ctrl+L write on connect.
Most TUI apps and shells repaint on Ctrl+L, avoiding the PTY size
dance. Revert HandleResize to plain syncSize.

refactor(clone): make Serial/Console pointer types, strip stale paths

Changed chVMConfig Serial/Console from value to pointer (nil = omit
from JSON). patchCHConfig now strips snapshot's stale /dev/pts/N paths
and sets nil before rebuilding based on boot mode. Removed the Ctrl+L
injection (didn't help reliably). Updated buildCLIArgs and
runtimeFiletoCLIArg for pointer semantics.

fix(clone): set serial/console config based on boot mode

Added directBoot to patchOptions so patchCHConfig can set the correct
serial/console pair: OCI gets console=Pty, cloudimg gets serial=Socket.
Previously the mode detection was incorrect after stripping stale paths.

feat(clone): regenerate kernel cmdline for OCI clones

Added buildCmdline to generate kernel boot parameters with the clone's
VM name, IP, and DNS servers. Added vmName/dnsServers to patchOptions.
Also fixed localfile.Create to persist the Image field in snapshot
records.

feat(clone): patch stale disk paths in state.json

Build old-to-new disk path mapping from the original CH config and
patched storageConfigs. Apply string replacement in state.json so
embedded disk_path values reflect the clone's paths. This is
informational only (CH opens disks via config.json) but prevents
debugging confusion.

fix(clone): update bootCfg.Cmdline for subsequent restarts

After patching config.json, also update the in-memory bootCfg.Cmdline
so that VM restarts (not just the initial restore) use the clone's
identity (VM name, IP, DNS).

fix(clone): preserve CH device IDs by patching config in-place

Network and balloon patching now updates fields in-place instead of
rebuilding the slice/struct, preserving CH-assigned device IDs
(e.g. "_net3"). Added ID field to chNet, chDisk, and chBalloon.
Added net count mismatch validation. Removed unused prefixToMask.

feat(clone): resource inheritance, cidata regeneration, and UX

Major clone enhancements:
- CloneVMConfigFromFlags: inherit CPU/Memory/Storage from snapshot,
  validate clone resources >= snapshot minimums
- CloneNICsFromFlags: enforce NIC count matches snapshot device tree
- Separate addCloneFlags (0/empty = inherit from snapshot)
- Extract generateCidata for reuse between Create and Clone
- Cloudimg clone: regenerate cidata and ensure it's in storageConfigs
- Snapshot captures CPU/Memory/Storage/NICs; list shows resource columns
- localfile.Create stores full SnapshotConfig (not field-by-field copy)
- Print post-clone setup hints (balloon cache drop, network reconfig)

refactor(clone): raw JSON patching to preserve CH internal fields, add tests

Rewrote patchCHConfig to use a dual-parse approach: typed struct for
validation, map[string]json.RawMessage for writing. This preserves CH
internal fields (platform.uuid, cpus.topology, memory.thp, disk
pci_segment, etc.) that were silently lost by the old marshal/unmarshal.

Extracted all patch functions to patch.go. Fixed updateCOWPath to return
error when no COW disk matches. Fixed localfile.Restore to return
CPU/Memory/Storage/NICs fields.

Added clone_test.go (16 tests) covering patchCHConfig, updateCOWPath,
rebuildStorageConfigs, rebuildBootConfig, patchStateJSON. Added Restore
roundtrip tests to localfile_test.go.

utils: make ForEach concurrent using errgroup

VM start/stop/delete operations were serialized because ForEach
iterated sequentially. Use errgroup with optional SetLimit to run
operations concurrently while preserving best-effort semantics.

hypervisor: pass PoolSize to ForEach for bounded concurrency

Convert forEachVM to a method on CloudHypervisor so it can read
PoolSize from config. VM start/stop/delete operations are now
bounded by the configured pool size instead of running unbounded.

hypervisor: default PoolSize to NumCPU when unset

Normalize PoolSize=0 to runtime.NumCPU() in forEachVM, matching
the OCI layer processing convention and the config's documented default.
Without this, zero PoolSize meant unlimited goroutines.

utils: make ForEach/BatchResult generic, add Map for concurrent mapping

ForEach[T] and BatchResult[T] now work with any type, not just strings.
Map[T,R] provides fail-fast concurrent mapping (used by OCI pull/import,
replacing inline errgroup patterns). Config.EffectivePoolSize() centralizes
the PoolSize-to-NumCPU fallback that was duplicated in 3 call sites.

support firecracker as hypervisor backend (#16)

* feat: add --fc persistent root flag for Firecracker backend selection

Add --fc flag to select Firecracker as hypervisor backend.
Validates mutual exclusion with --windows and rejects cloudimg
(UEFI boot) since Firecracker only supports direct kernel boot.
InitHypervisor dispatches based on config; FC returns stub error
until the backend is implemented.

* feat: add hypervisor/firecracker package skeleton

Create Firecracker backend package with Config (path helpers),
main Firecracker struct (constructor, Inspect, List, Watchable),
and helper utilities (toVM, path functions). Wire up InitHypervisor
to create FC backend when --fc is set. Lifecycle methods are stubs
pending implementation.

* feat: implement Firecracker Create + Start lifecycle

Add FC REST API client (pre-boot config model), Create (COW disk +
device-path cmdline), and Start (launch process → REST API config
sequence → InstanceStart). FC references disks by /dev/vdX path
since it lacks virtio serial support. Update overlay.sh init script
to resolve both device paths and serial names.

* feat: implement Firecracker Stop and Delete

Add Stop (SendCtrlAltDel → SIGTERM → SIGKILL) and Delete
(stop-if-running → cleanup dirs → remove DB record) for the
Firecracker backend. Follows the same patterns as CH.

* feat: implement Firecracker Console with PTY + Unix socket relay

FC binds serial to process stdin/stdout. Create PTY pair at launch:
slave → FC stdin/stdout, master → background relay process. The
relay (self-exec with env var detection) listens on console.sock
and bridges connections to the PTY master. Auto-exits when FC dies.
Console() connects to console.sock, consistent with CH backend.

* feat: implement Firecracker Snapshot, Clone, and Restore

Add full snapshot lifecycle for FC backend:
- Snapshot: pause → PUT /snapshot/create (vmstate+mem) → reflink COW → resume
- Clone: extract → launch new FC → PUT /snapshot/load → reconfigure drives/NICs → resume
- Restore: kill running → extract → new FC → snapshot/load → reconfigure → resume
- Direct: hardlink mem, reflink COW, copy vmstate for local snapshots

FC snapshot/load does not preserve drive/NIC config, so drives and
networks are re-attached after load. Implements hypervisor.Direct
interface for reflink-optimized local snapshot operations.

* feat: add Firecracker detection and install to doctor/check.sh

Add FC_VERSION variable (v1.12.0), firecracker binary detection in
check_binary, and auto-install from GitHub releases in --upgrade mode.

* docs: update README with Firecracker backend documentation

Add --fc flag to global flags, Firecracker section with feature
comparison matrix, limitations, OCI image compatibility notes.
Update requirements, doctor, VM lifecycle, and shutdown behavior
sections to reflect dual-backend support.

* fix: FC launch issues found during e2e testing

- Pre-create FC log file (FC requires O_WRONLY|O_APPEND, no O_CREATE)
- Use underscores in drive/iface IDs (FC rejects hyphens)
- Add vmlinux extraction from vmlinuz (FC needs uncompressed ELF kernel)
- Support zstd and gzip compressed kernels via CLI decompressor
- Fix FC download URL in doctor/check.sh (tarball format)

* fix: address code review findings from /simplify

- Guard boot pointer nil dereference in prepareOCI
- Fix relayBidirectional goroutine leak: buffer 2, close conn, wait
- Optimize ensureVmlinux: check ELF magic (4 bytes) and cache before
  reading full vmlinuz into memory
- Extract magic strings to constants (driveIDFmt, ifaceIDFmt,
  cowFileName, FC action types, VM state strings)
- Deep-copy SnapshotIDs map in toVM to prevent shared DB mutation
- Return real error from decompressZstd when output is empty

* refactor: extract shared Backend struct and helpers to hypervisor/

Extract ~650 lines of duplicated code from CH and FC backends into
shared hypervisor/ layer:

- Backend struct with BackendConfig interface: provides Inspect, List,
  ToVM, ResolveRef(s), LoadRecord, WithRunningVM, UpdateStates,
  MarkError, ReserveVM, RollbackCreate, ForEachVM, AbortLaunch
- shared.go: EnterNetns, WaitForSocket, ExtractBlobIDs, BuildIPParams,
  PrefixToNetmask, CopyFile, RemoveVMDirs, CleanupRuntimeFiles,
  BlobHexFromPath, SocketPath, ConsoleSockPath
- config.HypervisorType enum + switch-case in InitHypervisor
- FC version updated to v1.15.0

* fix: handle CopyFile writable file close error

* fix: address P1/P2 review findings from PR #16

P1 GC: Implement RegisterGC for FC backend — protects blob IDs
referenced by FC VMs from garbage collection, mirroring CH's GC module.

P1 Clone paths: Save cocoon.json metadata (StorageConfigs + BootConfig)
in snapshot tar. Create temporary symlinks from source drive paths to
clone paths before snapshot/load so FC finds drives at expected locations.
Symlinks are cleaned up after load + reconfigure.

P2 Rebuild: Replace fragile rebuildFromSnapshot (searched live VM records)
with self-contained metadata from cocoon.json. Clones no longer depend
on the source VM or any sibling VM existing in the DB.

P2 Console relay: Add 3s timeout on second goroutine wait after client
disconnect to prevent blocking the accept loop when PTY read is stuck.

* fix: GC registers both backends, doctor optional FC, debug rejects --fc

P1: GC now registers ALL hypervisor backends (CH + FC) via
InitAllHypervisors, protecting blobs from both backends on
mixed-backend hosts regardless of --fc flag.

P2: doctor/check.sh treats firecracker as optional — warns instead
of failing when not installed, since it's only needed for --fc.

P3: vm debug rejects --fc with a clear error since it only generates
Cloud Hypervisor launch commands.

* fix: clone always redirects source COW, snapshot stores portable kernel path

P1: createDriveRedirects now unconditionally redirects the source COW
path to the clone's copy. When the source VM is still running, its
cow.raw is renamed to a temporary backup, a symlink is placed, and
after snapshot/load the backup is restored. This prevents FC from
reopening the live source VM's disk state.

P2: saveSnapshotMeta stores the portable vmlinuz path instead of the
host-local vmlinux cache. cloneAfterExtract runs ensureVmlinux on
the clone host to (re)create vmlinux from vmlinuz, making FC
snapshots fully portable across hosts.

* fix: abort clone on redirect failure, store portable relative paths

P2 redirect: createDriveRedirects now returns error. On symlink
failure after backup rename, the backup is immediately restored
and all prior redirects are cleaned up, preventing source VM disk
corruption from a half-installed redirect.

P2 portable paths: snapshot metadata (cocoon.json) now stores paths
relative to root_dir using filepath.Rel. loadSnapshotMeta resolves
them against the local host's root_dir. Snapshots exported from one
host can be imported on another with a different Cocoon directory
layout, as long as the same OCI image has been pulled.

* fix: persist hypervisor type in snapshots, serialize COW redirects

P1: SnapshotConfig now carries a Hypervisor field ("cloud-hypervisor"
or "firecracker") set during Snapshot(). Clone validates that the
snapshot's backend matches the active backend before proceeding,
with a clear error suggesting the correct flag.

P2: COW redirect during clone is now serialized via a per-source-COW
flock (.clone.lock). Concurrent snapshot/restore/clone operations on
the source VM block until the redirect is cleaned up, preventing
them from following the temporary symlink to the wrong disk.

* fix: include source COW path in snapshot metadata

saveSnapshotMeta now stores ALL drive entries (RO layers + RW COW),
not just RO entries. Without the source COW path, createDriveRedirects
had no old→new mapping to redirect, so snapshot/load would reopen
the live source cow.raw (if source VM exists) or fail (if deleted).

* fix: vmstate-aware redirects, COW lock in snapshot/restore, lock dir creation

P1: acquireCOWLock (via lockCOWPath) now creates the parent directory
before locking, fixing ENOENT when source VM has been deleted.

P2: snapshotMeta stores SourceRootDir. vmstatePaths() reconstructs
the original absolute paths baked into FC's vmstate binary.
createDriveRedirects uses vmstate paths as symlink targets, so
cross-host clones redirect at the correct (source host) paths.

P2: COW flock is now taken in Snapshot and Restore too (via shared
lockCOWPath helper), not just Clone. Concurrent snapshot/restore
operations on the source VM are serialized with clone redirects.

* fix: Codex review — GC fail-fast, atomic vmlinux, zstd dep, relay redesign

P1: InitAllHypervisors now returns error instead of silently skipping
failed backends. GC aborts if any hypervisor can't be loaded, preventing
blob deletion when pinning data is incomplete.

P2: ensureVmlinux writes to a temp file and renames atomically,
preventing concurrent readers from observing a truncated kernel cache.

P2: Added zstd to doctor/check.sh binary checks — required by FC's
kernel decompression but was previously an undeclared dependency.

P2: Redesigned console relay to use a single persistent PTY reader
goroutine with broadcaster pattern. Each session subscribes/unsubscribes
via setSink(). No per-session read goroutines on the PTY master,
eliminating stale goroutine data theft after disconnect.

* fix: Codex review round 2 — vmstate paths, optional zstd, stop flags

P1: vmstatePaths() now reconstructs from raw relative paths saved
before local resolution, so cross-host clones correctly redirect
at source-host paths even when root_dir differs.

P2: zstd treated as optional in doctor/check.sh (like firecracker),
warns instead of failing on CH-only hosts.

P3: FC Stop now honors --force (skip SendCtrlAltDel, immediate kill)
and --timeout (wait for guest response before escalating). Added
gracefulStop with SendCtrlAltDel → poll → forceTerminate pattern.

* fix: self-deadlock in GC Collect — use lock-free DB access

GC orchestrator holds the module's flock for the entire cycle. Collect
called LoadRecord which called DB.With → locker.Lock on the same flock,
causing self-deadlock since flock is not re-entrant.

Replace LoadRecord (lock-acquiring) with DB.ReadRaw (lock-free) in both
FC and CH GC Collect. This is safe because the GC orchestrator already
holds the lock, preventing concurrent DB mutations.

* fix: replace IP=dhcp with IP=off in initramfs to fix boot and network issues

IP=dhcp caused three problems:
1. --nics 0 VMs hung forever (dhcpcd retries every 120s with no interface)
2. DHCP network VMs had leases persisted as static configs by
   systemd-network-generator, breaking DHCP semantics on reboot
3. Source VMs and cloned VMs had inconsistent network behavior

IP=off tells initramfs to skip networking entirely. Kernel ip= parameters
(when present for static IP networks) override this setting and still
trigger ipconfig. DHCP networks rely on systemd-networkd via the existing
20-wired.network (DHCP=yes) fallback, or cocoon-network's MAC-based
DHCP config generation.

fix: give vm.snapshot / vm.restore a 10-minute heavy-op timeout

The CH REST client utils.NewSocketHTTPClient sets http.Client.Timeout
to 30 seconds, which fires regardless of any context.WithTimeout at
the call site. vm.snapshot and vm.restore write/read the entire VM
memory image; on multi-GiB Windows snapshots over GCE standard
persistent disk, or for mid-boot snapshots still dirty with Windows
init activity, 30s is marginal and occasionally exceeded.

DoWithRetry masks the symptom by retrying 4x, but each attempt hits
the same 30s ceiling, so the user-visible effect is a ~2-minute wait
followed by "Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers".

Fix: add heavyClient(hc) that clones the caller's http.Client by
value and raises Timeout to 10 minutes. The Transport (socket dialer
and connection pool) stays shared, so light endpoints like vm.pause
and vm.resume still use the original 30s client unchanged. Only
vm.snapshot and vm.restore route through heavyClient.

10 minutes was chosen to give multi-GiB cold-start restores real
headroom on slow disks while still bounding a genuine CH hang. The
global HTTPTimeout stays 30s to keep fast endpoints responsive.

fix: deterministic VM ref routing with ambiguity detection

hypervisorConstructors was a map, so InitAllHypervisors iterated in
random order. FindHypervisor / RouteRefs probed backends first-success-
wins, meaning the same VM name in two backends would non-deterministically
resolve to either — vm stop / rm / restore / console could silently hit
the wrong backend.

Replace the map with an ordered hypervisorFactories slice and add a
new resolveVMOwner helper that (a) distinguishes ErrNotFound from real
backend read errors and propagates the latter, and (b) collects every
match and returns hypervisor.ErrAmbiguous when >1 backend owns the
same ref, forcing the user to disambiguate instead of silently picking
one.

fix: cloudimg clone preserves base image blob pinning

cloneAfterExtract recomputed blobIDs via ExtractBlobIDs on storage
configs rebuilt from the VM's config.json. For a cloudimg clone those
configs hold the clone's writable overlay path, not the base qcow2
blob path, so ExtractBlobIDs returned a digest derived from the
overlay filename — not the actual base image hex. The clone's VMRecord
then pointed ImageBlobIDs at that garbage hex, and GC's referenced-set
scan no longer saw the real base image as pinned. A subsequent GC pass
could delete the base blob the clone's qcow2 backing file chain still
depends on.

Drop the recomputation. ReserveVM in cloneSetup already pinned
snapshotConfig.ImageBlobIDs when the clone record was created, and
those IDs were captured correctly at snapshot time.

fix: restore filters cidata disk for post-first-boot cloudimg

buildVMConfig drops the cidata disk on subsequent starts of a cloudimg
VM (cloud-init has already consumed it). A snapshot taken after that
has [overlay] only in config.json, but rec.StorageConfigs still keeps
[overlay, cidata] because the VM record is never updated to reflect
the post-first-boot state.

Restore passed rec.StorageConfigs straight to patchCHConfig, which
hard-fails on the 2-vs-1 disk-count mismatch — AFTER prepareRestore
has already killed the running VM, leaving the user with a torn-down
VM and no path forward.

Extract an activeDisks(rec) helper that applies the same filter, and
use it in both buildVMConfig and restoreAfterExtract so the launch
and restore paths see a consistent view.

fix: ListAllVMs surfaces backend read errors instead of hiding them

The old loop dropped list errors with a silent continue, so a corrupt
or transient-failing backend DB would hide every VM from that backend
in vm ls / vm status output without any indication. Propagate the
error instead — users can retry or repair the affected backend, and
half-fleet-visible states are no longer possible.

fix: image ref ambiguity detection and owner-targeted rm

Image refs were not globally namespaced but ResolveImage silently
picked the first backend that resolved a name, and image rm iterated
every backend and called Delete on each — so same-named entries in
both OCI and cloudimg would be (a) silently shadowed on create/run
and (b) both destroyed by a single rm. Neither behavior matches user
expectations.

Add images.ErrAmbiguous sentinel. ResolveImage now probes all backends
and returns the sentinel when >1 match. New ResolveImageOwner helper
returns the sole owning backend (errors on ambiguity or not-found).
image rm now resolves owner per ref and deletes only from that one
backend.

fix: reject cpu > host cores at create/clone/restore entry points

buildVMConfig silently clamped rec.Config.CPU to runtime.NumCPU() when
the request exceeded host cores, but the VM record, snapshot config,
and inspect output kept the original request. Network queue counts
were derived earlier from the unclamped value (network/cni/create.go),
so disks ran with clamped queues while NICs ran with unclamped queues
— three views of "CPU" all out of sync.

Add shared hypervisor.ValidateHostCPU helper and call it at every
entry point that accepts a new VMConfig: CH Create, cloneSetup (covers
Clone and DirectClone), Restore, DirectRestore; FC Create, cloneSetup,
Restore, DirectRestore. Remove the silent clamp in buildVMConfig — by
the time it runs rec.Config.CPU has already been validated and all
downstream consumers see a single coherent value.

fix: restore stages snapshot extract before killing running VM

Both CH and FC Restore used to kill the running VM + delete cowPath +
extract tar into rec.RunDir. A truncated or corrupt snapshot stream
would therefore error out AFTER the previous runnable state was
already torn down — the user was left with no VM and no path forward.

Extract into a sibling scratch dir (runDir + ".restore-staging")
BEFORE killing. Only if extract succeeds do we kill the VM and swap
staged files into runDir via a new hypervisor.MergeDirInto helper
(per-file rename, same-filesystem assumption). A bad stream now
errors out with the running VM still alive.

Split prepareRestore into resolveForRestore (no kill) + killForRestore
(destructive, marks VM as error on partial kill failure). DirectRestore
still uses the combined prepareRestore wrapper since it consumes a
pre-extracted local dir.

fix: importQcow2File verifies digest match across two read passes

importQcow2File hashes the user file in Pass 1 and copies it into a
cocoon temp in Pass 2. If the user modifies the source file in place
between the two reads (TOCTOU window), the digest is computed from
the old bytes while the temp file holds the new bytes — commit would
then store and index content under a digest that does not match its
own body.

Hash the source during Pass 2 too via io.MultiWriter and compare to
the Pass 1 digest; fail on mismatch. Zero extra I/O — the second
sha256 runs inline in the copy.

fix: concat sniff accumulates >=8 bytes across shards

importQcow2Concat's inline first-file sniff called sniffImageSource
on file[0] alone. If file[0] was shorter than 4 bytes, sniff returned
a "too small to be a disk image" error even when the concatenated
stream was a valid qcow2. Worse, signatures needing 6 bytes (xz, 7z)
would pass prefix detection on a 4-5 byte file[0] that joined with
file[1] into a rejectable archive.

Extract sniffConcatHead helper that reads across shards until 8 bytes
are accumulated (or all files exhausted), then hands the buffer to
sniffHead. Move the sniff call out of the copy loop to a pre-copy
check for symmetry with the other import entry points.

fix: restore clears staging dir to avoid replaying stale files

The stage-extract refactor used a fixed <runDir>.restore-staging path
and MkdirAll, which is a no-op when the directory already exists. An
abrupt exit (SIGKILL, panic, power loss) between ExtractTar and
MergeDirInto leaves files in staging that the deferred RemoveAll
never cleans up. The next restore's ExtractTar only overwrites
entries present in the new tar — orphan files from the previous
attempt stay. MergeDirInto then renames every file (new + orphan)
into rec.RunDir and the restored VM boots with a poisoned state.

RemoveAll the staging dir before MkdirAll on entry so each restore
starts from a clean slate. Both CH and FC restore paths need the
fix — same pattern.

fix: image inspect detects cross-backend ambiguity

The previous ambiguity fix covered ResolveImage and image rm but
missed Inspect, which still looped backends in fixed order and
returned the first non-nil match. A ref that existed in both OCI
and cloudimg stores was silently resolved to whichever backend
came first (OCI), hiding the collision from the user.

Route Inspect through the existing ResolveImageOwner helper so
cross-backend collisions surface as images.ErrAmbiguous the same
way they do for create/run/rm.

hypervisor: data disk creation pipeline behind --data-disk

User-facing flag --data-disk lands. Each value is parsed as
size=20G[,name=...][,fstype=ext4|none][,mount=/mnt/x][,directio=on|off|auto];
omitted name is filled with dataN, omitted mount with /mnt/<name>, omitted
fstype with ext4. fstype=none requires empty mount. Names cap at 20 chars
to match Linux's virtio by-id truncation, and the cocoon- prefix is
reserved.

hypervisor.PrepareDataDisks creates each <runDir>/data-<name>.raw via
OpenFile+Truncate (PrepareOCICOW pattern; os.Truncate would not create),
mkfs.ext4 reuses InitCOWFilesystem. fstype=none leaves the file unformatted.

Both backends append data disks after their writable rootfs disk:
  - CH OCI:        layers... + cow + data...
  - CH cloudimg:   overlay + data... + cidata
                   (cidata stays last so activeDisks() filtering after
                    first boot doesn't shift devPath of data disks)
  - FC OCI:        layers... + cow + data...

Snapshot/clone/restore still see only the new disks as raw files; the
follow-up commits make them roundtrip correctly.

cloudhypervisor: persist Role/MountPoint/FSType via cocoon.json sidecar

CH writes a cocoon.json sidecar inside every snapshot tar that mirrors
config.json's disk shape — same order, same length — but carries the
cocoon-only fields (Role, MountPoint, FSType, DirectIO) that CH's schema
cannot.

Sidecar is built by parsing the snapshot's just-written config.json,
then looking each disk path up in rec.StorageConfigs. This deliberately
avoids activeDisks(rec): a cloudimg VM snapshotted between FirstBooted=true
and the next stop still has cidata attached in CH's view, so config.json
shows it; activeDisks(rec) would not, breaking the sidecar/config.json
length invariant patchCHConfig depends on.

Clone reads the sidecar, validates it through ValidateStorageConfigs
(may come from imported snapshots, untrusted), then proceeds with the
StorageConfigs already carrying full Role/MountPoint/FSType. The old
rebuildStorageConfigs helper and roleFromCHDisk Role-from-chDisk inference
are removed; the sidecar makes them unnecessary. The TestRebuildStorageConfigs
fixture is dropped along with them.

direct.cloneSnapshotFiles needs no change: cocoon.json falls into the
Meta classifier and is plain-copied into the clone's runDir.

storage: include data disks in snapshot tar; clean stale ones on restore

Snapshot now reflinks each Role==Data disk into the staging dir during

streamed/direct clone places them at the new runDir. CH and FC follow
identical patterns; data disks are not subject to FirstBooted filtering,
so they're enumerated directly off rec.StorageConfigs rather than via
activeDisks().

cleanSnapshotFiles matchers in both backends' direct.go now include
data-*.raw so a restore (which goes kill-VM → clean → reflink) cannot
leave stale data disks from a previous incarnation alongside the freshly
extracted ones. CH also cleans the cocoon.json sidecar; FC already had
its sidecar in the matcher under a different name.

firecracker: lock all writable disks of a source VM, not just the COW

withSourceCOWLocked only held the COW lock; with data disks added, a
concurrent snapshot reflinking those same files races against a clone
that renames+symlinks them via createDriveRedirects. The new helper
collects every Role==COW || Role==Data path, sorts by string, and
locks them sequentially via withCOWPathLocked. The dictionary order
guarantees concurrent callers acquire locks in the same sequence, so
deadlock is impossible. recoverStaleBackup runs once per path after
its lock is held, matching the previous semantics for the COW.

clone.go's call site switches to the new helper; snapshot.go replaces
its bare withCOWPathLocked(cowPath, ...) the same way. The old
withSourceCOWLocked is removed.

storage: harden restore preflight and FC writable-disk lock

Three findings from review, all confirmed real:

P1: CH/FC preflight let snapshots through even when CH state.json,
memory-range-*, FC vmstate, mem, COW or cidata files were missing.
killForRestore would already have run by the time vm.restore /
snapshot-load actually noticed, costing an outage on a malformed tar.

  - hypervisor.ValidateSnapshotIntegrity now stats every snapshot-resident
    file in the sidecar (Role==COW, Cidata, Data) by basename. Layers are
    shared blobs, not in srcDir, so they're skipped.
  - cloudhypervisor.validateSnapshotIntegrity adds state.json + at least
    one memory-range-* check on top of the common preflight.
  - firecracker.preflightRestore adds vmstate + mem checks on top of the
    common preflight (cow.raw is covered by the sidecar walk now).

P1: FC restore / DirectRestore only locked the COW path. With data disks,
a previous clone that crashed mid-redirect could leave a stale
data-<x>.raw.cocoon-clone-backup. Restore happily wrote a new
data-<x>.raw next to it, then the next clone or snapshot acquired that
disk's lock, ran recoverStaleBackup, and renamed the backup back over
the freshly restored data — silently corrupting it.

  - Both restore paths switch to withSourceWritableDisksLocked(rec.
    StorageConfigs, ...), which already runs recoverStaleBackup on every
    writable disk (COW + Data) in dictionary order. Stale backups get
    healed before the restore touches the disks, and held locks block
    concurrent clone/snapshot from racing the swap.

cloudhypervisor: assert sidecar/config.json disk order in preflight

writeSnapshotMeta builds the sidecar by walking chCfg.Disks in order, so
sidecar[i] and chCfg.Disks[i] must agree on Path and ReadOnly. We already
validated count, structural fields, file presence, and role sequence, but
left the per-index identity unchecked.

A drifted sidecar (tampered, partial overwrite, snapshot built by an
older cocoon version) would have slipped through preflight; clone's
patchCHConfig would then have written each sidecar entry's path into the
wrong disk slot, leaving CH device state pointing at the wrong files.

Per-index Path + ReadOnly comparison closes the gap; cost is one short
loop. Role is not on chCfg, so it stays out of this check.

support clone and restore from specific dir (#22)

* snapshot: extract ReadSnapshotEnvelope shared helper

Move the canonical snapshot.json envelope read/write into the snapshot
package so cmd/vm can consume an envelope-bearing directory directly
(needed for the upcoming \`vm clone --from-dir\` and
\`vm restore --from-dir\` paths) without depending on localfile internals.

- snapshot.SnapshotJSONName + envelopeVersion (single const block).
- snapshot.ReadSnapshotEnvelope(dir) parses + version-checks; returns
  ErrEnvelopeMissing when the file is absent so callers can surface a
  precise message instead of a generic open error.

- localfile/export.go now references snapshot.SnapshotJSONName.
- localfile/import.go readAndRemoveSnapshotJSON delegates the parse to
  the shared helper; remove-after-read semantics preserved.

* snapshot: add export --to-dir for directory-based handoff

Adds the snapshot.DirectoryExporter optional interface and a
LocalFile.ExportToDir implementation. The dir form pairs with the
upcoming \`vm clone --from-dir\` and \`vm restore --from-dir\`,
giving users an rsync-friendly handoff path without a tar round-trip.

- snapshot.DirectoryExporter: ExportToDir(ctx, ref, dir) error
- LocalFile.ExportToDir: rejects non-empty target dirs to avoid silently
  merging into an unrelated tree, writes a fresh snapshot.json envelope
  via WriteSnapshotEnvelope, then ReflinkCopy's each data file. Reflink
  is zero-cost on btrfs/xfs and falls back to plain copy elsewhere; the
  result is always standalone (rsync-friendly), unlike the hardlinks
  DirectClone uses internally for memory pages.
- cmd/snapshot: --to-dir flag, mutually exclusive with --output/--gzip.

* vm: clone --from-dir for arbitrary snapshot directories

Lets users clone from any directory containing a snapshot.json envelope
(e.g. an extracted export.tar, an rsync'd \`snapshot export --to-dir\`
result, or an NFS-mounted golden image) without first registering the
snapshot in the local DB.

- cloneCmd args relaxed to MaximumNArgs(1); positional SNAPSHOT and
  --from-dir are mutually exclusive (validated in the handler so the
  error message names both forms).
- cloneFromDir reads the envelope, routes to the matching backend by
  cfg.Hypervisor, asserts hypervisor.Direct, then funnels through the
  same DirectClone path as the snapshot-DB form.
- cloneDirect refactored to share cloneFromSrcDir with cloneFromDir so
  the prepareClone → DirectClone → finalize sequence isn't duplicated.

The dir is read-only across the call so multiple clones of the same dir
(golden image use case) are safe. Trust boundary unchanged: existing
ValidateMetaPaths still rejects envelopes whose storage paths escape
the local rootDir/runDir.

* vm: restore --from-dir with --force ownership gate

Symmetric with \`vm clone --from-dir\` but with an extra safety check:
the envelope's snapshot ID must belong to vm.SnapshotIDs unless --force.
This keeps the typical cross-host "sync the same VM's backup over here"
flow zero-friction while making "use unrelated state to overwrite this
VM" an explicit, opt-in operation (data-loss footgun otherwise).

- restoreCmd args relaxed to RangeArgs(1, 2); positional SNAPSHOT and
  --from-dir are mutually exclusive (handler-validated).
- restoreFromDir reads the envelope, resolves the VM's hypervisor,
  asserts hypervisor.Direct, runs the same NIC-count + resource-flag
  validation as the snapshot-DB form, then DirectRestore over the dir.
- --force does NOT add the envelope's ID to vm.SnapshotIDs — restoring
  doesn't change ownership semantics, the foreign snapshot remains
  external to this VM's lineage.

* docs: --from-dir + --to-dir directory-based snapshot workflow

Bullet point in features + extended export flag table + a worked example
covering the three flows: golden image clone, cross-host same-VM
restore, force-overriding a foreign-lineage restore.

* style: trim verbose godoc on the new envelope/clone/restore paths

Comments per SKILL.md should explain WHY, not narrate or restate the
signature. This pass keeps the load-bearing rationale (atomic write
reason, soft-gate semantics, reflink-vs-hardlink trade-off) and
collapses the rest.

* snapshot: write envelope last in ExportToDir as completion marker

ExportToDir wrote snapshot.json before copying payload files. A
concurrent \`vm restore --from-dir\` reading the envelope could pass
preflight (which only stat()s presence, not byte-completeness) and kill
the running VM while a memory-range or COW file was still mid-copy,
leaving the source VM in Error state with a partial restore.

Move WriteSnapshotEnvelope to after the copy loop so envelope existence
is now an all-data-ready marker. ensureEmptyDir already guarantees the
dir starts empty, so a stale envelope can't survive into the new
export.

Returning *types.SnapshotConfig forced an awkward

chain forced \`return &cfg\` / \`*cfg\` / \`&cfg\` dances at every layer.

Switch to value semantics inside the cmd-layer + snapshot-backend
boundary; the hypervisor backend interface (Clone / DirectClone) keeps

single deref happens at that boundary. SnapshotConfig is small (no

Mirrors the DataDir flip: the snap-DB-side Restore was the only place

Clone and Restore had near-identical mutex / required-arg blocks; the

fix(snapshot): fall back to non-sparse tar when segment map exceeds PAX cap (#23)

Go's archive/tar caps the encoded PAX block at maxSpecialFileSize =
1<<20 (see archive/tar/format.go). Our sparse encoding stuffs the
entire sparse-segment list into a single COCOON.sparse.map PAX record,
which is fine for typical disk images but trips the cap when the
underlying file is highly fragmented.

Reproduced 2026-05-05 against a live cocoon Windows VM running the
simular-pro-agent-runtime 1.8.0 build (Electron app, real Firebase
WebSocket signed-in): the agent's V8 heap + IPC + WebSocket pools
fragment the guest memory enough that memory-ranges yields tens of
thousands of sparse segments; the resulting JSON exceeds 1MB and
`cocoon snapshot export` fails with:

    Error: write archive: write header memory-ranges:
        archive/tar: header field too long

vk-cocoon then loops indefinitely retrying the push (see
project_cocoon_sparse_pax_overflow memory note in vm-service tree),
silently breaking hibernate.

The fix detects the overflow up front (mapJSON > ~800KB, well below
the 1MB cap) and falls back to writing the file as a regular,
non-sparse tar entry. This loses the sparse-export size advantage on
the affected file (memory-ranges can be GB-scale), but those files are
not the dominant size driver in a snapshot — and a successful larger
push beats a hung loop. Empirical Go-tar limit measured: 30k segments
(~736KB JSON) succeed, 50k (~1.2MB) fail.

Reader path is unchanged. The fallback emits a standard tar entry that
existing extract logic already handles via the non-sparse code path.

Tests:
  - TestTarFileMaybeSparse_FallsBackOnLargeMap — verifies the fallback
    triggers when the map exceeds the cap and that no PAX sparse
    records are written.
  - TestTarFileMaybeSparse_FallbackRoundTrip — extract of a
    fallback-encoded file matches the original byte-for-byte.
  - TestTarFileMaybeSparse_PreservesSparsePathForSmallMaps — sanity
    that small fragmentation still uses the sparse encoding.

* fix: vm logs -f handles backend log truncation across stop/start

Both backends'\'' start paths reopen the VM log with O_TRUNC (same inode),
so a follower whose fd was past the previous EOF would silently miss
everything the new boot writes until the file grew past the old offset.

Compare current fd position against the file'\''s current size on every
fsnotify event; if size shrunk, seek back to 0 before io.Copy so the
new boot'\''s log is replayed from byte 0.

* fix: vm logs uses persisted VMRecord.LogDir, doc clarifies truncate

to b.Conf.VMLogDir for legacy records that predate LogDir persistence).

that doesn't hold the running VM's actual log.

* fix: make streamLog io.Copy context-aware for prompt Ctrl-C cancellation

* docs: clarify -f seeks to start on truncation rather than reopening the file

* fix: detect log truncate-then-regrow via head signature, drop ctx wrap

Codex review on PR #29 surfaced a real race: when stop+start truncates
and regrows the log to the same byte length within the 100ms WatchFile
debounce window, info.Size() < pos is false and the size-only rewind
misses the new boot's lines entirely. Repro: deterministic CH boot
warnings, follower stuck at old EOF, new boot's timestamped lines
silently dropped.

Switch the regen check to a head-signature compare: ReadAt the first
64 bytes (CH/FC stamp a unique boot timestamp at line 1) and rewind
when the signature changes. ReadAt doesn't move the fd position, so
the catch-up io.Copy continues from where it left off when no rewrite
occurred.

hypervisor logs are KB-scale, not a critical path, and the parent ctx
already cancels the surrounding select; chunked copying was over-

parent ctx is enough.

into utils.FileHead and reuse from both call sites.

it was just "share data" — and pass-by-value is hair cleaner: copies

(state already non-Running short-circuits IsProcessAlive), so neither

fix(metadata): netplan name-based fallback for cloudimg clone DHCP recovery (#34)

Append a "zfallback" netplan ethernet block (match by name=e*, dhcp4:true)

systemd-networkd processes the MAC-matched 10-netplan-id*.network files
first; the name-matched 10-netplan-zfallback.network only kicks in when
no idN matches — i.e. on a clone whose new MAC isn't in the snapshot's
netplan. DHCP-network cloudimg clones now self-heal at next boot;
static-IP cloudimg clones remain unchanged (no DHCP server to fall back
to is a network-mode limitation, not a software gap).

The post-clone hint claimed "DHCP networks: no action needed", but a
chained-clone Windows guest (snap → clone --on-demand → snap → clone
--on-demand) lands with the NIC bound at the OS layer, no IPv4, and
NDIS state inherited from the snapshot. The fix is a one-shot

NDIS bind and unsticks DHCP. cocoon-agent over vsock survives the
stuck NIC, so the rebind can be driven from the host.

`-PresentOnly` is load-bearing: chained-clone images accumulate
ghost Net PnP entries from earlier MAC generations, and Disable-
PnpDevice on a non-Present device returns HRESULT 0x80041001
(Generic failure) and aborts the pipeline before reaching the

fix(exec): make vsock CONNECT handshake honor ctx so Ctrl+C unblocks

The CH/FC hybrid-vsock CONNECT handshake reads `OK <port>\n` from the
host UDS byte-by-byte. The unix conn is accepted by CH the moment we
dial, but if cocoon-agent inside the guest is not yet listening on the
target port (cold-boot race, restart loop, crashed service), the OK
reply never arrives and the read blocks indefinitely on the syscall.
SIGINT / SIGTERM into the cocoon CLI gets delivered into ctx but
nothing was watching it, so user-level Ctrl+C did nothing — observed
stale `cocoon vm exec` processes piling up over multiple test runs.

Pass ctx into dialHybridVsock and arm context.AfterFunc to close the
conn on cancel; the blocked Read returns with err, we surface ctx.Err
in preference. exec_test.go updated to pass context.Background.

Validated: `timeout 5 cocoon vm exec <stuck-vm> dir` now returns at
5s with `dial agent: context canceled`, instead of hanging until the
process is forcibly killed.

fix(image): force-pull when digest pinned but missing locally (#39)

* fix(image): force-pull when digest pinned but missing locally

EnsureImage already proves at the first Inspect call that the requested
ImageDigest isn't in the local cache. The subsequent Pull, however,
passed force=false and so hit the URL-level short-circuit in
images/cloudimg/pull.go that skips re-downloading when "any blob is
already cached under this URL." For mutable tags (e.g. epoch's /dl/
endpoint pointing at the latest push of a repo), the cached blob can
be a stale digest — exactly the scenario that left clones failing
downstream in vm.restore with a "Backing file I/O error" against a
qcow2 backing file whose digest doesn't exist on disk.

Pass force=true to Pull when ImageDigest is set. Cheap path (no digest
pinned) stays cheap. Slow path triggers only when the caller wants a
specific digest and we've shown it isn't local — same semantics users
already get from `cocoon image pull --force`.

feat(gc): add --snapshot LRU eviction flag (#53)

Adds opt-in snapshot reclamation to `cocoon gc`:

  --snapshot                evict every non-pending snapshot
  --snapshot-keep N         keep N most-recently-accessed
  --snapshot-age DUR        evict last-accessed older than DUR
  --snapshot-size SIZE      evict oldest until total <= SIZE
  --dry-run                 preview without acting

Sub-flags combine as a union of evictions (intersection of kept) —
a snapshot survives only if it passes every active criterion. Bare
`--snapshot` (no sub-flag) nukes all non-pending, useful for dev
resets. Mixing sub-flags without `--snapshot` errors out.

now: without -i the child's stdin closes immediately; -i attaches the
caller's stdin. Pipelines like 'echo x | cocoon vm exec vm -- cat' need
-i from now on.

feat(vm): atomic hibernate; restore accepts stopped VMs

vm hibernate captures like snapshot save but terminates the VMM inside
the pause window instead of resuming, so the snapshot point and the
stop coincide and nothing written after the snapshot is lost on resume.
Restore's running-only guard relaxes to running-or-stopped: the
sequence cold-spawns a fresh VMM from the snapshot either way and the
kill step already tolerates a dead one. Restore paths keep the
entropy-only reseed, so a resumed VM retains its machine identity.

fix(vm): hibernate persists before killing the VMM

The previous order terminated the VMM and marked the VM stopped before
the snapshot reached the store; a failed save (disk full, snapshot DB
error) then closed the TarDirStreamWithRemove stream, deleting the only
memory image — VM stopped, no resume point. Persist now runs inside the
pause window and the VMM dies only after it succeeds: any failure up to
that point resumes the VM and the command simply fails. Hibernator
takes the persist callback so the hypervisor layer stays ignorant of
snapshot storage. Also updates README/KNOWN_ISSUES for hibernate and
restore-on-stopped.

fix(vm): roll back the recorded snapshot id when hibernate persist fails

RecordSnapshot runs before persist, so a persist failure resumed the VM
but left a snapshot id in the record that maps to nothing. Drop it via
best-effort UnrecordSnapshot on that path, and cover both hibernate
sequence outcomes with unit tests driven by a stub VMM process.

test(vm): fix stub-VMM exec race; cover terminate failure; fold persist tail

cmd.Start returns before bash execs into the argv[0]-renamed tail, so
the cmdline liveness check raced on Linux (green on darwin only via the
no-/proc fallback) — poll until the check passes. Add the third
hibernate outcome test (terminate failure marks error, snapshot stays
recorded). PersistSnapshotStream dedups the save/hibernate persist
tail; finishSnapshot inlined into SnapshotSequence.

fix(fc): re-anchor clone drives at their own paths after snapshot load

FC's snapshot/load reopens the drive paths embedded in the vmstate, so
clone satisfies them with temporary symlink redirects — but the loaded
VMM's device config keeps naming the source's paths. Any later snapshot
of the clone (vm hibernate, vm snapshot) embeds those dangling paths
and its restore fails with ENOENT on the source COW. PATCH /drives
after resume repoints each redirected drive at the clone's canonical
path (same inode, so the guest sees nothing), making the clone's future
snapshots self-contained.

refactor(fc): derive redirect and re-anchor sets from one function

The fix's invariant — every redirected drive gets re-anchored — lived
in two textually-duplicated guards that could drift apart silently.

unit tests pin createDriveRedirects to it.

fix(vm): keep a stopped VM restorable after a transient restore failure

A hibernated (stopped) VM whose restore failed transiently was marked
error, and ResolveForRestore refuses error-state VMs — the wake was
permanently bricked until the lease reaped it. FailRestore now spares a
stopped origin at the two sequence-level failure exits: nothing ran,
record and snapshot are intact, and a retry converges. The run-dir-
mutating steps (staged merge, direct populate) still quarantine
unconditionally — a partial merge or clean-then-clone leaves mixed-
vintage files that vm start must never boot. origin is the pre-kill
state, since metering may flip the DB record to stopped after the kill.

fix(vm): spare a stopped origin when the restore kill step fails

KillForRestore marked the VM error on any non-ErrNotRunning failure,
including WithRunningVM's fail-closed /proc-scan error. For a hibernated
(stopped) VM the VMM is provably gone — hibernate marks error if its
terminate fails — so a transient scan hiccup during wake bricked a
perfectly restorable VM: ResolveForRestore refuses error state, and
nothing on disk had been touched. Route the failure through FailRestore
(#89's origin-aware helper): stopped origins stay stopped and the wake
remains retryable; a failed kill of a genuinely live VMM on a running
origin still quarantines.

Closes #102, #103.

vm disk attach now persists an External StorageConfig on the record:
the volume survives stop/start (start rebuilds args from the record,
with a deterministic device id so list/detach keep working) and rides
hibernate/wake transparently — the guest resumes with the volume still
mounted. Snapshots carry only the reference: ReflinkDataDisks and the
snapshot-resident check skip External entries, and integrity validation
stats the absolute path instead. Sidecar external entries are trusted
only against the live record's external path set — a foreign snapshot
cannot name arbitrary host files, and clones of volume-referencing

run dir, dies with the process): device attach/detach, net resize,
snapshot, hibernate, restore, stop-before-delete. Device prechecks read
vm.info under the lock, closing the same-path/different-name concurrent

android: default redroid display refresh to 60fps (#105)

redroid guest mode leaves the display HAL at its 15fps default, so the UI feels laggy even though the software renderer draws a frame in ~1ms and host CPU stays under 10% — this is why Android felt slow while a Windows VM on the same host did not.

The image's init-wrapper defaults to 60fps and honors kernel cmdline redroid.fps=N for override. Measured at 4C4G: scroll fps 14.5 -> 58.7 (~4x), jank 0.24%, host CPU 93% idle. 60 is the sweet spot (the HAL halves 90 to 45). Refresh rate is a redroid-image concern, so the fix lives entirely in the image; cocoon stays image-agnostic.

* cni: attempt every NIC teardown before the DB sweep

The old always-sweep rationale (stale record blocking resize-up) doesn't hold: with a lingering interface the CNI ADD fails loudly either way, and a duplicate record is released idempotently at vm rm.

New Remove-level test drives teardown-failure -> sweep -> retry against a real store.

Review follow-up closing the remaining compensation gaps:

vm rm (deleteVM) and GC swept every record even when its CNI DEL failed, so a record kept by a failed detach was still lost one layer later — the IPAM leak just moved. Both now sweep only the released records; a failure is retried on the next GC cycle.

Resize-up had no reconcile entry: Add ran a fresh CNI ADD against an index whose stale record (and IPAM lease, keyed by container+ifname) survived a failed detach — host-local refuses the duplicate allocation. Add now reclaims the stale record first (DEL by the record's own conflist, best-effort TAP delete, sweep), which also heals the pre-existing lease collision that existed under the old always-sweep behavior.

A failed reclaim can leave two records for one ifname (old lease still tracked + fresh add). Remove's byIfName map collapsed them non-deterministically, stranding the loser as a phantom until vm rm. Pick every matching record instead — DEL is idempotent, and evicting the stale record at Add-insert would untrack the unreleased lease, recreating the original leak.

* cni: idempotent TAP delete; reclaim keeps record on TAP failure

Review follow-up on the TAP state machine:

deleteTAPInNetns treated an absent TAP (LinkNotFoundError) or an already-deleted netns (NSPathNotExistErr) as failure, so every teardown retry after a partial failure — the exact scenario the kept-record design exists for — wedged on the missing device and the record could never converge (Remove retry, duplicate-record sweep, and GC's post-netns-removal cycles alike). Absent now means success.

reclaimStaleNIC ignored TAP-delete failures and swept the record anyway: a lingering TAP then collided with the re-add's CreateTAP with nothing left to retry the cleanup. Any failure now keeps the record; both DEL and TAP delete are idempotent, so the next re-add retries safely.

* cni: fail resize-up when the stale reclaim fails

Warn-and-continue after a failed reclaim had no good outcome: a strict IPAM plugin fails the ADD anyway (burying the root cause), and a lenient one double-allocates so the user sees a successful resize-up that never reconciled. Reuse the index only after a full reclaim; the error is retryable since the whole reclaim chain is idempotent.

* cni: cover Add's fail-closed reclaim; fold reclaim into tearDownNICs

Mutation testing showed no test caught reverting Add's fail-closed reclaim — Add had no unit test at all because ensureNetns/setupTCRedirect are linux-only. Put both behind the existing seam pattern and add an Add-level test driving reclaim-failure -> fail-closed -> retry -> fresh record.

reclaimStaleNIC duplicated tearDownNICs's conflist+DEL+TAP sequence; it is now a thin wrapper (single record, sweep only what came back released), which also gives reclaim the same warn logging and idempotency semantics for free.

perf: parallelize the FC golden-clone burst path (#123)

* perf(fc): release the source-disk lock once snapshot/load holds the drive fds

Burst clones of one golden serialized on the source COW flock across
launch, snapshot/load, resume, and re-anchor. FC resolves the redirected
source-absolute paths only during snapshot/load and holds the drive fds
once it returns, so the redirect window is all the lock must cover:
launch moves before the lock, resume and re-anchor run after release.

* perf(clone): skip fsync on placeholder index writes

PrereserveVM and the CloneSetup adoption both rewrite the full VM index
through ReserveVM, each paying tmp fsync + parent-dir fsync for a
placeholder whose loss on power failure only re-exposes resources the GC
orphan sweep already reclaims. Route them through a new UpdateNoSync;
FinalizeClone/FinalizeCreate stay durable, preserving the durable-prefix
property (any later synced write persists earlier mutations too).

* perf(fc): bind-mount clone redirects in a private mount namespace

The symlink-redirect dance mutates the source paths in the host
namespace, forcing sibling clones of one golden to serialize on the
source-disk flock for the whole snapshot/load. Bind-mounting the clone
disks over the source-absolute paths inside a private mount namespace
leaves the host untouched, so concurrent loads need no lock at all.
The namespace rides a throwaway locked thread (Go threads share
CLONE_FS, so the thread cannot rejoin the pool) and dies with FC.
Missing or symlinked sources and unshare-denied environments fall back
to the existing locked redirect path, which also heals crash leftovers.

* perf(clone): skip the reseed re-inspect when the record carries VsockSocket

Clone and restore already return records with runtime sockets set, so
the extra full-index Inspect per clone only pays off when the field is
empty.

* review: move bindableRedirects below the Firecracker method set

* review: fold the simplify round

Drop bindableRedirects' derivable bool; compose load and resume under
startCloneVM so cloneAfterExtract keeps a single MarkError block.

* review: close the codex round — never-torn index writes, bind-detach verification

Codex flagged two holes. UpdateNoSync skipped the temp-file fsync, so on
a filesystem without auto_da_alloc a power loss could tear the whole VM
index, not just drop the placeholder; the write now keeps the file fsync
and skips only the parent-dir one (UpdateNoDirSync) — content is old or
new on any filesystem, and only the rename can roll back. And unlinking
a mountpoint path from another namespace detaches the bind
(mount_namespaces(7)), so a source restore/delete racing the unlocked
bind→load window could hand FC the source's writable disk; after load
the clone now verifies every redirected clone inode is among the VMM's
open fds and aborts cleanly otherwise.

* review: harden the codex residuals

Reject duplicate bind destinations (a shared dst inode would mask a
detached sibling bind in verifyDriveFDs) and state UpdateNoDirSync's
journaled-filesystem contract.

* fc: mark the symlink fallback for bind-only unification

Production runs cocoon as root on the host, so the unshare-denied case
is a bench-rig artifact; once mount-ns has soaked a release the dead
source case can bind over a locked placeholder mountpoint instead,
retiring the rename/symlink/backup machinery.

perf(store): move Update fsyncs out of the flock hold (#126)

* perf(store): move Update fsyncs out of the flock hold

Sixteen-way clone bursts drain the VM-index flock as a staircase: every
holder pays the file and parent-dir fsync inside the hold, so waiters
queue behind stable-storage flushes (strace: 13/29 contended flock
attempts, all fsync time in-hold). Update now renames under the lock
and fsyncs after release — callers still return only once durable.
Because the rename is unsynced, a crash can tear the fresh index on
filesystems without rename-over data ordering; writeRaw therefore
hardlinks the durable previous generation to <index>.prev (metadata
only) before renaming, and load falls back to it loudly when the main
file no longer decodes. Recovery keeps its promises narrow: a recovered
main is never rotated into .prev (it is the torn one), read errors fail
closed so a transient EIO cannot serve stale state, and the post-release
fsync covers .prev too, closing the double-tear window when the previous
writer died before its own fsync.
Measured on the testbed: FC burst16 wall 131-167 -> 86-106ms, per-clone
p50 -32%, burst64 p50 608 -> 467ms; serial unchanged; torn-index e2e
recovers loudly.

* review: close the review-round on the store crash contract

Update composes UpdateNoDirSync so the .prev fsync covers both paths;
the .prev rotation goes link+rename so a recovery generation exists at
every instant (remove-then-link left a window with none); a double
decode failure reports both errors; and the interface states the
declared crash contract — the residual multi-writer window (all racing
relaxed writers killed before their post-release fsyncs, then power
loss) survives as old-or-new only under ext4-class rename-over data
ordering, the deployment filesystem.

* review: fsync main before .prev so a belt failure cannot strand the caller's generation

feat(vm): replace --on-demand with --restore-mode copy|ondemand|mmap (#127)

* feat(vm): replace --on-demand with --restore-mode copy|ondemand|mmap

CH's restore API takes one memory_restore_mode enum; a bool flag can only
reach one of its three values. --restore-mode passes the value through
(empty/copy omits the field, preserving the wire default), adding the new
mmap mode: CoW-map the snapshot memory file so clones of one snapshot
share page cache — measured on 16 cores: 16-way clone burst per-clone p50
450ms -> 79ms vs copy. ondemand/mmap require the snapshot file to remain
on disk; mmap additionally requires it unchanged for the VM lifetime.

--on-demand is removed rather than aliased: it mapped to the same field
and CH-side gains nothing from a second spelling.

* docs: restore-mode needs a CH build with matching support

An older CH has no memory_restore_mode field and serde silently ignores
it, restoring by copy while reporting success; say so instead of gating

fix(vm): tolerate processes vanishing mid /proc scan (#129)

* fix(vm): tolerate processes vanishing mid /proc scan

A process exiting between the /proc readdir and its cmdline read made
ScanProcsByBinary fail the whole scan and vm rm refuse the delete: the
scan skipped ENOENT (gone before open) but not ESRCH (reaped between
open and read). Gate the fail-closed path on IsProcessAlive instead of
errno matching: a gone process cannot hold VM resources, whatever errno
its disappearance surfaced.

fix(cni): quiesce host NICs on stop to end the idle-TAP softirq storm (#130)

* fix(cni): quiesce host NICs on stop to end the idle-TAP softirq storm

A stopped CNI VM keeps its netns/TAP for a fast restart, but the VMM exit
drops the TAP's carrier while its veth stays up on the host bridge; the tc
mirred redirect then fires against the down TAP for every LAN broadcast
packet ("mirred to Houston: device is down"), storming softirqs (NOHZ
tick-stop) until the host soft-locks and reboots. Teardown only ran on vm
rm, so any stopped CNI VM was a host-crash landmine. Bring the veths down
on stop (Quiesce) and back up on start (Unquiesce) so the redirect never
targets a carrier-less TAP.

* clean

* clean

* fix(cni): also quiesce on vm rm --force, not only vm stop

vm rm --force kills the VMM (dropping the TAP's carrier) but only removes
the netns/TC redirect afterwards via netProvider.Delete, leaving the same
idle-TAP softirq storm window vm stop had — long enough to crash a host on
a busy bridge. Extract stopAndQuiesce and reuse it from rm --force before
the delete.

fix(oci): decompress gzip arm64 kernel on import for CH direct-boot (#134)

* fix(oci): decompress gzip arm64 kernel on import for CH direct-boot

Cloud Hypervisor on arm64 can only direct-boot a raw kernel Image, but Ubuntu
ships the arm64 vmlinuz gzip-compressed. Passing it as --kernel makes CH treat
it as a UEFI payload and fail with UefiLoad(UefiTooBig). Gunzip the kernel when
extracting boot files on arm64; x86 bzImage is not gzip and is copied verbatim.

* fix(oci): bound arm64 kernel decompression against a gzip bomb

The gzip path added an unbounded decompression surface (G110): a crafted small
vmlinuz could inflate to exhaust the host boot cache. Cap the decompressed
kernel at 512 MiB (real kernels are under 100 MiB) and error out past it.

fix: harden cocoon for sub-1500-MTU / high-vCPU cloud hosts (CH rlimits + CNI MTU/MSS) (#135)

* fix(ch): raise RLIMIT_MEMLOCK/NOFILE before launching the VMM

Cloud Hypervisor allocates an io_uring ring plus eventfds per virtio-blk queue,
and num_queues scales with vCPU, so a high-vCPU multi-disk guest (e.g. an 8-vCPU
10-disk Android VM = 80 queues) exhausts the default RLIMIT_MEMLOCK (~memlock) and
RLIMIT_NOFILE (1024), failing disk activation with 'AsyncIo: I/O error' then
'Too many open files' VMM panic. Lift both before fork; the VMM inherits them.

* fix(doctor): match CNI bridge MTU to host egress + clamp forward MSS

On a host whose egress MTU is below the CNI bridge default 1500 (GCP is 1460),
guests silently blackhole large DF packets (TLS/data), so e.g. reaching a CDN with
a big cert chain times out while ping/small requests work. Set the bridge mtu to
the detected host MTU in the generated conflist, and add a mangle FORWARD
TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu rule so existing hosts are fixed without bridge rebuild.

* Clean up comments in start.go

Remove unnecessary comments about VMM resource limits.

* fix(hypervisor): raise VMM rlimits in the shared launcher to cover Firecracker

The rlimit raise sat in the CH-specific launch path, but Firecracker also forks a
VMM with an io_uring block engine (IoEngine=Async) and hits the same
RLIMIT_MEMLOCK/NOFILE exhaustion. Both backends go through Backend.LaunchVMProcess,
so raise the limits there, right before spec.Cmd.Start().

fix(vm): bound the best-effort reseed after clone/restore (#139)

* fix(vm): bound the best-effort reseed after clone/restore

reseedAfterResume fires a CRNG reseed over the guest's hybrid-vsock on the
command's background context. When the guest vsock is unreachable — e.g. a
hypervisor that resets virtio-vsock on restore, leaving the agent silent —
the CONNECT reply read (dialHybridVsock) or the reseed frame read blocks
forever, hanging `vm clone` / `vm restore` despite reseed being documented
as best-effort and non-fatal.

Bound each dial+reseed attempt with reseedAttemptTimeout so the signal
degrades to a warn within a fixed budget instead of wedging the command.

* remove notes

* Format constants in reseed.go for consistency

chore: bump Firecracker baseline to v1.16.1 (#143)

FC v1.16.0 snapshot-restore leaves the guest's virtio-vsock silent
forever (#140): host CONNECTs reach the guest but no reply ever comes
back, so the agent and silkd are unreachable on every restored or cloned
VM. v1.16.1 fixes the restore path upstream; A/B on the same cocoon
binary and image confirms restored clones answer exec again.

fix(ch): restore clone NICs onto throwaway taps to end the tap-attach races (#142)

vm.restore recreates net devices from the snapshot's config.json, whose
tap field still names the source VM's tap: concurrent clones of one
golden race to attach that single tap and lose with EBUSY (1/16 at
B=16). Retargeting restore at the clone's real taps is no fix either —
vm.remove-device releases a tap only after the guest ACKs the eject, so
the later hot-swap add-net EBUSYes on its own tap. Patch each restored
NIC onto a clone-unique throwaway tap instead: CH auto-creates it at
restore, the hot-swap replaces it with the real NIC, and the kernel
destroys it when the ejected device drops its fd.

fix(ch): fail fast when an mmap restore would silently degrade to eager copy (#144)

CH's CopyOnWrite restore needs plain private-anon guest memory; on
hugepage or shared-memory snapshots it logs a warn and falls back to
eager copy while reporting success. cocoon auto-enables hugepages
whenever the host has nr_hugepages > 0, so a golden built on such a host
silently loses the entire CoW density/latency win on every clone.
Reject an explicit --restore-mode mmap against an incompatible snapshot
in clone and both restore preflights instead of degrading.

meta: unified metadata layer P0+P1 — record-granularity store, json engine, tombstone protocol (#147)

Squashes the design/meta-store review branch into the implementation
branch; issue #146 carries the summary, this document is canonical.

* meta: record-granularity metadata API with json engine and contract suite

P0 boundary of the meta-store design (issue #146): Scope-declared
transactions with a single write namespace, per-transaction CommitMode
with structural durability enforcement, detached values, Collection/Log

daemon: optional resident supervisor for cocoon-managed VMs (#152 P0+P1) (#154)

* hypervisor: transition generations and the supervision seam

Every committed state write now goes through markTransition, which stamps a
dense transition_generation plus reason and timestamp on the record. The
generation is what lets a supervisor fence an observation against a record that
moved on since: without it, an exit seen before a restart could date or re-label
the newer transition.

ConvergeDead lands the stop transition for a VMM that exited outside a cocoon
stop, closing the compute interval only when one is open — a legacy Running
record with no interval still converges, without emitting an unmatched stop.
quiesce_pending survives a crash between that transition and the network
quiesce, so a later pass retries it; setting it rides the durable commit and
clearing it is relaxed, since a lost clear only costs one idempotent re-quiesce.

CollectStaleCreate extracts GC's stale-create protocol so a caller holding the
ops lock can run it without the age gate.

* cmd: run network convergence inside the VM ops lock

recoverNetwork and quiesceNetwork lived in the command layer, outside the lock
the hypervisor takes for start and stop. That left two windows open: a stop's
late quiesce could bring down plumbing a concurrent start had just brought up,
and a crashed VM's TAP kept its tc redirect because only the stop path quiesced
at all.

Both now run through an injected NetLifecycle inside StartSequence,
StopOneLocked, HibernateSequence and restoreCore. A failed recovery aborts
before launch instead of booting a VM with half-built networking.

NetProviders replaces the per-call provider caches the command layer threaded
around; NewGCOrchestrator lifts the collector registration gc and the daemon
both need.

* daemon: resident supervisor for cocoon-managed VMs

cocoon daemon adopts the VMM processes the CLI launched and converges what a
crash leaves behind: an open compute interval, a record still reading running,
and a TAP whose tc redirect storms softirqs. Every CLI verb keeps working with
no daemon running.

Exits are detected with pidfd and epoll, fenced by both the process generation
(pid plus start time) and the record's transition generation, so an event
queued before a restart can never stop the VM that replaced it. The reconcile
ticker is the correctness floor for anything the watcher missed, including
exits during downtime; meta events only make passes sooner, debounced because
the json engine's View holds a cross-process namespace lock.

A creating placeholder whose ops lock is free has no live owner — create and
clone hold it from prereserve through the final commit — so it is collected at
once, freeing the name reservation instead of waiting out the GC grace.

The read-only API over a unix socket exposes health, the supervised set, and an
SSE change stream. It replays nothing: a reconnecting client compares per-VM
transition generations against the opening snapshot to find what it missed.
Restart policy stays with the consumer; the daemon only reports.

* docs: daemon guide

* meta, cni: survive a namespace dir and a netns that do not exist

Two paths only a resident supervisor exercises hard enough to hit.

The json engine's Events added an fsnotify watch per namespace directory and
failed the whole subscription if any was missing. A namespace whose owning
backend has not run yet — snapshots on a fresh root — has no directory, so the
daemon silently degraded to ticker-only reconciliation. Missing directories are
now skipped; the safety poll already covers them and a later subscribe picks
the watch up.

CNI Quiesce entered the VM's netns unconditionally. A host reboot wipes every
netns while the records survive, so after the pending-quiesce flag made the
failure durable, every VM would have retried a doomed quiesce on every pass
forever. A netns that is gone has no plumbing left to bring down.

The daemon now logs the first events failure and the recovery, not every retry.

* ch: default clones to the mmap restore fast path (#157)

Clones of plain private-anon snapshots (no hugepages, no shared) now

snapshot GC: the mapping taken at vm.restore keeps the file's inode

artifacts, and export orders data before its snapshot.json marker.

vmlock: transient lease files with GC sweep for the residue (#167)

* vmlock: transient lease files with GC sweep for the residue

Lease files accumulated forever: VM IDs are ULIDs, every VM ever
created left a permanent empty file under locks/vm, and deletion was
unsafe because a naive unlink splits the lock across two inodes.

Adopt the transient flock pattern vmlock-wide: an exclusive release
unlinks the file while still holding it (flock.NewTransient), and
SharedLease re-verifies after acquiring LOCK_SH that its fd is still
the inode bound to the path, reopening when a transient release
unlinked it mid-wait — without that rebind an exclusive unlink would
strand a waiting lease on an orphaned inode and the SH/EX interlock
would silently split. Ops locks now self-clean on every release; the
only residue left is lease files whose last holder was a shared lease
(dead-source clones), swept by a new vmlock GC module that skips IDs
any backend still knows and anything still locked.

Hot-path cost: two stats on acquire, one unlink on release.

cloudhypervisor: converge a VM left paused by a killed capture (#176)

* cloudhypervisor: converge a VM left paused by a killed capture

A `snapshot save` or `hibernate` killed inside its pause window leaves the guest
frozen with nobody left to resume it: WithPausedVM's resume runs on the way out,
and a SIGKILLed process never gets there. Every later device op then failed on
that stale pause, because ensureNotPaused refused outright:

    Error: vm is paused (snapshot or hibernate in flight); retry after it completes

For vk-cocoon that was terminal. Its resumed hibernate re-runs `vm net --nics 0`
first, which was already a no-op (the NIC had been dropped before the save), and
the refusal happened before the target==current early return -- so the wedge was
reachable through the ordinary `systemctl restart vk-cocoon` path and needed a
hand-written vm.resume on the API socket to clear.

Paused observed by these callers has no owner, and that is provable rather than
assumed: every pause window in cocoon runs under the VM ops lock end to end
(prepareSnapshot, prepareRestore), clone resumes a record still in creating which
runningVMClientWithRecord rejects, and all three ensureNotPaused callers already
hold that same lock. So a caller holding the lock cannot be racing a live
capture. convergeOrphanedPause resumes and returns a re-read vm.info, which
callers need since they classify devices off it. resumeVM was already idempotent,
and pauseVM already carried the mirror-image fix ("swallows CH's Paused->Paused
500 so a stuck-paused VM recovers") -- the capture path anticipated this, the
device path did not.

Verified on internal-cocoon-node-7: stop vk 3s into a save, then restart. The
resumed hibernate now reports hibernate_total{netresize,ok} and runs through
snapshot/push/remove to Suspended, where the old build logged netresize failures
until the pod was abandoned. The guest marker written before the hibernate was
present after the wake.

snapshot: make the save name preflight read the index the insert enforces (#177)

* snapshot: make the save name preflight read the index the insert enforces

`snapshot save --name X` checks the name twice through two lookups that disagree
about pending records:

- EnsureSnapshotNameFree goes through Inspect, whose lookupRecord rejects
  `r.Pending` and reports not-found;
- insertRecord goes through the raw name index, which a pending record holds.

A save killed after beginCreate but before finalizeCreate leaves exactly that
pending record: rollbackCreate is cancel-proof but not SIGKILL-proof. Its name
then looks free to the preflight and taken to the insert, so the save runs the
whole capture -- a multi-GB memory dump plus disk copy -- and only then fails
with `already in use by <ID>`. Retries repeat the capture every time; a real
incident left 14 GiB of abandoned capture dirs behind.

The preflight now consults the name index directly through a new optional
NameHolder interface (same shape as Direct/DirectCreator), so a taken name is
rejected in under a second, and the message names the holder so a caller can
remove it by ID -- name resolution is not guaranteed to reach a pending record.
Backends that do not implement it keep the Inspect path.

This does not make the pending record self-collecting: GC still owns that, with
pendingGCGrace at 24h. It only moves the rejection before the expensive work and
makes it actionable. The vk-cocoon side removes the holder and retries.

* snapshot: collect a dead save's pending record on lease proof, not age

Every save holds its snapshot's exclusive build lease from placeholder
to finalize and the flock dies with the holder, so a pending record
whose lease GC can acquire is provably ownerless — the same free-lock
proof vm stale-create collection uses. GC already takes the exclusive
lease before every collect; dropping the 24h age gate from candidate
selection and revalidation makes a killed save's name and capture dir
reclaimable on the next pass instead of a day later. A live save is
never collectable: its held lease fails the try-acquire.

Bridge.Add issued eight netlink calls per NIC — LinkAdd, LinkByName, master,

vm: keep qcow2 overlays buffered so a shared base stays in the page cache (#194)

* vm: keep qcow2 overlays buffered so a shared base stays in the page cache

Cloud Hypervisor used to open a qcow2 backing file with buffered I/O no
matter what the disk asked for, so the shared base image behind every
cloudimg and Windows VM was served from one host page-cache copy. It now
opens the backing file with the disk's own direct flag, and cocoon sets
direct=on for every writable disk, so each VM started reading the base
image straight from storage instead.

Default direct=off for a qcow2 that layers over a base image. The
overlay itself loses O_DIRECT, so its writes land in the host page cache
as well as the guest one. That memory is reclaimable, and the residual
cost is one extra copy per written byte, which is the cheaper half of
this trade: without it every VM refetches the shared base from storage.
Raw COW disks, read-only layers and data disks are unchanged, and an
explicit direct_io on a data disk still wins.

Expressing the split the old Cloud Hypervisor gave us by accident, a
direct overlay above a buffered base, needs a per-backing-file cache
policy that no released version has. That is requested upstream in
cloud-hypervisor/cloud-hypervisor#8718.

Measured on a 16-core host with a 700 MiB base image and 8 VMs reading
1 GiB each: base image resident in the page cache 310 MiB with the fix
against 0 MiB without it, aggregate read 1.86s against 2.47-2.67s.

* firecracker: advertise the TAP MTU to the guest

Cloud Hypervisor reads the TAP MTU and advertises it through

eth0 at 9000. Firecracker only advertises the feature when the NIC
config carries mtu (v1.16.0+), so the same VM on --fc stayed at 1500
and fragmented against the bridge. Both network providers now record
the TAP MTU on NetworkConfig (CNI from the veth inside the netns, the
bridge backend from the bridge) and the Firecracker backend sends it;
Cloud Hypervisor keeps deriving it from the TAP.

A snapshot taken before nic_mtus was recorded advertised no MTU to its
guest, so every target network fits it; rejecting it for recording zero
NICs would break every Firecracker clone of an existing snapshot after
the upgrade. The clone-constraint docs name the MTU rule.
