A target network with a larger MTU than the snapshot would work, but
the guest would still run at the snapshot's MTU while the host side
expects the larger one; equality keeps clone behaviour predictable, so
the test now rejects both directions.

firecracker: opt-in virtio-pci transport (#217)

--pci on vm run/create starts Firecracker with --enable-pci so the guest
enumerates virtio-pci devices, the prerequisite for Firecracker device
hot-plug. The transport is recorded on the VM config, so clones and
restores relaunch on the transport their snapshot was taken with, and
Cloud Hypervisor rejects the flag since it is always virtio-pci. cocoon
no longer puts pci=off on the Firecracker command line: Firecracker adds
it itself whenever PCI is disabled (since the PCI work in 1.13, below the
1.16.1 floor), and on --enable-pci the flag would hide every device.

A Firecracker VM created with --pci now resizes NICs, attaches and
detaches raw disks, and takes --nics and --data-disk on clone the way a
Cloud Hypervisor VM does. The backend drives the virtio-pci devices
through GET /, GET /vm/config and PUT/DELETE on /drives and
/network-interfaces under the VM ops lock; MMIO VMs keep the explicit
rejection because only the PCI transport hot-plugs. Hot-attached disks
block snapshot and hibernate like on Cloud Hypervisor, use
cocoon_disk_<name> ids because Firecracker ids allow [A-Za-z0-9_] only,
and hot-added TAPs are single-queue, the only shape Firecracker opens.
A --pci clone restores every snapshot NIC through network_overrides
and resizes to --nics afterwards, once the clone's reservation lock is
released, and hot-plugs --data-disk files as the next drive slots so
later snapshots carry them as ordinary sidecar entries. Firecracker
delivers no hot-plug notification to the guest, so the CLI prints the
rescan and stale-node removal steps and returns them as hints in JSON.

vm: add --no-balloon; whole-repo comment, signature and layout round (#221)

* vm: add --no-balloon

Opts a VM out of the virtio-balloon (cocoon otherwise returns 25% of guest memory to the host with deflate-on-OOM). A guest that thrashes on page cache before the OOM killer fires never deflates: an 8-CPU/16G guest running a large TypeScript typecheck froze with 11.5G used and a 4G balloon inflated. patch list (patchOptions) has no balloon field and vm.restore rebuilds the
device tree from snapshot state, and FC's putBalloon runs only on the cold-boot
path. A clone flag therefore changed the record while the live device kept
following the snapshot, and the next cold start silently switched it.

perf: coalesce tar extraction into one write or seek per run of blocks (#225)

extractFile issued one write or one lseek per 4 KiB block for the whole
entry, so a hole-free multi-GiB memory file (tarred through
rewindAndTarFull with no sparse map, the shape a warm VM produces) cost
about 262k syscalls per GiB on the tar restore, clone and stream-create
paths. It now reads up to 1 MiB (bounded by the entry size), scans the
same 4 KiB sub-blocks for zeros, and turns each run of data blocks into
one write and each run of zero blocks into one seek; hole granularity
and the trailing Truncate are unchanged. The per-entry sync.Pool around
the old 4 KiB buffer goes with it.

cocoon-test2 (XFS on NVMe), 2 GiB entry, 30 percent zero blocks, five
reps per arm interleaved, both orders: production median 1.53-1.63 s
with 365,125 writes; coalesced median 0.32-0.40 s with 3,205 writes and
2,359 seeks, identical sha256. Pooled versus per-entry buffers on 20,000
4 KiB entries: 31 vs 33 us per entry.

fix: derive disk queue affinity from the VM's own cpuset placement (#226)

* fix: derive disk queue affinity from the VM's own cpuset placement

queueAffinity mapped queue i onto host CPU i whenever a VM had no placement,
and Cloud Hypervisor turns that into sched_setaffinity on every virtio-blk
queue worker. Each VM on a host therefore produced the same mapping and the
whole population's COW queue threads piled onto the lowest core ids. The
cgroup_cpus fence does not help: it is machine-wide, so falling back to it
relocates the pile-up instead of removing it. Only an explicit per-VM
cpuset_cpus is a core set this VM owns alone, so that is now the only source;
without one no affinity is emitted and the scheduler places the threads.

Clone and restore drop the snapshot's queue_affinity before re-deriving, so a
source host's mapping cannot survive onto a node that does not want it.

Measured on a 384-core host, 24 concurrent 8-vCPU sandboxes with 8 in-guest
O_DIRECT writers each, arms interleaved A-B-B-A x3 with zero failures: before,
cpu0-7 ran 96-99% busy while cpu8-383 sat at 4-6%; after, 19-26% and 27-30%.
4k throughput 377 -> 969 MiB/s (2.57x), and the delta is 9x the A/A spread. No
change where the device is the limit (1M blocks hold 3.88 GiB/s in both arms)
or on cold claims (912 vs 903 ms p50, inside the A/A spread).

* review: give queueAffinity the whole pinning rule and rehome PlacementCPUs

The cpu>1 half of "when do we pin a queue" was written at both call sites
while the placement half already lived in queueAffinity; fold it in so one
owner holds the rule and one test case pins it.

PlacementCPUs is a config-derived helper for start, clone, restore,
DiskAttach and the debug CLI, so it belongs in utils.go beside HostCPUCount
and ValidateHostCPU rather than in the start operation's file, and it gains
the direct test the deleted EffectiveCPUs used to have.

* review: close the queue-affinity coverage gaps and unify the assertions

Three behaviours the round found unpinned: the unconditional delete now
strips a read-only disk's stale mapping too, both clone hot-plug sites feed
the placement through, and queueAffinityToCLI renders it. Each new assertion
was checked by reverting the code it guards.

The affinity table now compares with sameQueueAffinity like its sibling in
clone_test.go instead of a parallel [][]int and a hand-rolled loop, and
PlacementCPUs drops an error branch ParseCPUList never takes, matching how
cgroup.go already spells the same call.

fix: a listening API socket is not a launched VM; reject an invalid queue size (#227)

cloud-hypervisor serves --api-socket before it parses the config it was launched with, and sends VmCreate and VmBoot as two separate requests behind it. WaitForSocket therefore returned success for a VMM that then exited: cocoon logged 'started' and exited 0 while the VM sat stopped and stale with an IP allocated. The CH PostLaunch hook now waits for vm.info to report Running, bounded by SocketWaitTimeout and failing fast when the VMM exits, so a dead or unbooted VMM takes the existing AbortLaunch path.

--queue-size and --disk-queue-size were bounded only from below, so a non-power-of-2 or oversized value reached the VMM verbatim and killed it at config validation. A virtio ring is a power of two no greater than 32768; 0 still means the backend default.

Verified on cocoon-test1 against v0.6.4: the released binary returns rc=0 with 'INF started' and leaves the VM 'stopped (stale)', while this build rejects the flag before any VM is created and fails the launch of a VMM that binds its socket and exits.

fix: derive the boot cmdline at start, not once at create (#228)

boot.Cmdline was materialised at Create/Clone and then replayed verbatim on every Start, while --net was already rebuilt from the live record. vm net --nics N updates NetworkConfigs only, so after a resize plus stop/start the guest came up on the address it was created with while the record and vm list reported the new one: the recorded IP unreachable, the guest holding a lease host-local IPAM lists as free. Both backends now rebuild the cmdline from the record they are about to launch — Cloud Hypervisor in buildVMConfig, Firecracker through the setBootCmdline its Create already used.

Verified on cocoon-test1 against v0.6.4 on both backends, including the --nics 0 to 1 variant, and vm debug output is identical between the two builds across seven VM shapes.

fix(ch): refuse a snapshot of a VM holding a vhost-user-fs or VFIO device (#229)

The snapshot pre-flight walked chCfg.Disks only, and could not have done more: chVMConfig declared no Fs or Devices field, so parseCHConfig never saw them. snapshot save therefore succeeded on a VM with a vhost-user-fs attached and produced a snapshot whose config.json names the virtiofsd socket; restoring it fails after 60s once the backend is gone and hangs indefinitely against a fresh one, leaving the VM in state=error. Cloud Hypervisor does not refuse the capture either, which is what docs/devices.md claimed.

chVMConfig now carries the Fs and Devices types the live path already had, buildSnapshotMeta refuses either with the detach hint the disk path gives, and hibernate inherits it through the shared spec. ErrHotAttachedDisk becomes ErrHotAttached, since it now covers three device classes.

Verified on cocoon-test1 against v0.6.4: the released binary captures the snapshot and the restore hangs; this build refuses the capture, still refuses a hot-attached data disk, and still snapshots and restores normally once the device is detached.

fix: reject a --from-dir snapshot whose raw COW is not the recorded size (#230)

cocoon's export tar stores sparse disks with private pax records (COCOON.sparse.size/map) that only its own ExtractTar understands: hdr.Size is the data length, so any other tar writes a file both truncated and shifted from the first hole on. ValidateSnapshotIntegrity only stats the disk files, so clone/restore --from-dir accepted such a directory, exited 0, and the guest read wrong data and logged EXT4-fs checksum errors. A same-lineage restore needs no --force, so an ordinary VM could be corrupted in place. docs/cli.md invited the sequence by saying the dir may be an extracted .tar; it now names the two supported flows.

Both --from-dir entry points cross-check cow.raw against the size the envelope records. The mainstream paths were never affected and stay verified: clone and restore from the store, snapshot import, and export --to-dir all keep cocoon's writer and reader on both ends.

Verified on cocoon-test2 with GNU tar 1.35 against v0.6.4: the released binary clones the corrupted directory and the guest marker's sha256 differs; this build refuses it, and all four supported flows still round-trip the marker intact.

fix(ch): wait for the vsock socket so vm run -o json carries it (#231)

SetRunningSockets gates vsock_socket on the UDS existing, and cloud-hypervisor creates it asynchronously after launch, so the post-start inspect usually lost the race: the released binary emitted the field in 1 of 30 runs on hardware. The CH PostLaunch hook now waits for the socket with the helper the launch path already uses for the API socket, bounded by the same timeout and failing fast if the VMM exits.

This says nothing about the guest agent being ready. Those are different states about 2.4s apart, and callers still retry exec exactly as before — measured on cocoon-test2, first successful exec at 2262-2475 ms on v0.6.4 and 2390-2440 ms on this build. What it buys is that a machine consumer no longer has to poll vm list to learn the path: 0/10 runs carried the field before, 10/10 after, at a cost of about 6 ms of median vm run latency.

feat: place disk queue threads by cache domain and add --cpuset-cpus auto (#235)

* feat: place disk queue threads by cache domain and add --cpuset-cpus auto

Cloud Hypervisor pins every writable virtio-blk queue worker with
sched_setaffinity, and since #226 only an explicit per-VM cpuset produced
a mapping, so the fleet's queue threads floated. Pinning is wanted: a
stationary worker keeps its io_uring state and its NVMe submission queue
on one core, and an I/O-bound vCPU is woken into that core's cache.
What was wrong before #226 was the mapping, not the pin: every VM used
the same 0..N-1 identity map and stacked onto one L3 complex.

Every launch (start, clone, restore) now derives the placement inside
one relaxed write transaction: it reads the host's last-level-cache
domains from sysfs, intersects them with the cgroup_cpus fence, counts
the pins the creating/running records already hold, takes the
least-loaded domain, and gives each queue its own hardware thread there,
distinct cores before SMT siblings. The transaction makes concurrent
clones see each other's pins, so a cold burst walks the domains instead
of piling up. The result lives on the record as queue_cpus, so hot-added
disks and vm inspect read the same set; a stopped VM holds none and the
next launch re-derives. An explicit cpuset keeps the #226 round-robin.

--cpuset-cpus auto reuses the same choice for the cgroup: the scope's
cpuset.cpus becomes the chosen L3 domain, so vCPUs, virtio workers and
io_uring threads share one cache while staying work-conserving inside
it. The resolved list is recorded as cpuset next to the request, and the
fence subset check and shrink refusal apply to it like any placement.

The clone hook now receives the placed placeholder record instead of
runDir/logDir/now, so both backends launch the record that carries the
placement. Firecracker records the auto domain but no queue pins.

Hot path: one relaxed write transaction per clone holding a record scan
plus about forty sysfs reads; measured against master on the testbed
with the A/B harness before merge.

* fix: make a recorded placement the load signal and count every backend

Two gaps in what placement counted as occupied cpus. Start and restore
place a record whose state is still Stopped, Created or Error until the
launch finishes, so the tally, which only read Creating and Running
records, could not see a VM that was spawning with those cpus and a
concurrent launch could take the same ones. And a VM with a cpuset but
no queue pins (Firecracker, single vCPU) never registered at all, so
every such --cpuset-cpus auto landed on the first domain.

The record's placement is now the signal itself: markTransition drops
cpuset and queue_cpus on every exit from Running and markFailedOperation
drops them after a failed launch, so a recorded placement means the VM
holds those cpus, whatever its state. The tally counts queue_cpus, or
the cpuset of a VM without pins, and scans the other backend's namespace
inside the same transaction, since both backends share one host. vm
inspect no longer hides the placement of a creating clone.

* fix: stamp a clone's start time at launch, not at reservation

RunningCloneRecord took CreatedAt, UpdatedAt and StartedAt from the
placeholder's CreatedAt, which a prereserved clone sets before the image
pull and the network setup, so a clone's uptime started before its VMM
existed. CreatedAt stays the reservation time; StartedAt and UpdatedAt
are stamped when the running record is built.

* review: queue placement round — hoist the sysfs walk, one scan loop, no debug pins

Applied from the whole-repo round on the merged tree:
- placeRecord reads the topology before taking the store's write lock;
  only the record scans and the write stay inside the serialized section.
- placementLoad scans the own and peer namespaces through one loop over
  a reader; placeVM takes a reader, not the transaction.
- Place ranks every thread by (layer within its core, load, id) and
  takes a prefix instead of building candidate lists layer by layer;
  ReadTopology returns early on a host without cache sysfs and filters
  the remainder in place.
- LaunchVMProcess takes the scope cpuset from the record alone; every
  launch path places first, so the fallback to the raw knob was dead.
- vm debug no longer renders a queue_affinity: placement happens at
  launch against the store, so a printed pin set never matched a launch.
- buildVMConfig parses the record's queue cpus once, not per disk;
  onlineCPUsPath derives from cgroup.SysCPURoot.
- Tests: the two-case affinity table becomes two asserts, ptr() gives way
  to new(false), TestFormatCPUList sits with the function it tests, and
  NewBackend's peer namespace wiring is pinned.
- Comments: the cores godoc restated its body; updateRelaxed's roster
  duplicated its callers; the placement invariant moves next to the
  clear it explains; the CPU knob header loses a clause AutoCPUSet
  already documents; the placement fields get their own group.
- Docs: fence shrink refusal covers cpusets, pins outside a new fence are
  widened until the next launch; the tally counts both backends and a
  pin-less VM's cpuset; Firecracker records the cpuset alone; single
  vCPU VMs never pin; vm debug and vm inspect state what they show.

* cut: fold CopyFile onto the exported copy helper

CopyFile re-implemented the open, create, copy and close sequence that
utils already owns for the sparse and reflink copies. The helper is
exported and CopyFile becomes its closure, keeping the source mode via
Chmod; a failed copy now drops the partial destination like the other
copies do.

* cut: drop the degenerate-name check ValidateMetaPaths already makes

Every caller of ValidateSnapshotIntegrity runs after LoadAndValidateMeta,
whose ValidateMetaPaths rejects a degenerate base name for every storage
config, and a data disk's resident name comes from the serial that
ValidateStorageConfigs on the first line of the same function checks.

feat: tally placements from a per-namespace row table (#236)

* meta(sqlite): add the tables a newer schema generation declares on open

Open keeps its contract of never creating or migrating. InitIfMissing,
which the composition root runs before every open, now also finds a
cocoon store stamped with an older generation and, under the init
flock, creates every declared table that is missing and stamps the
current generation in one transaction. Generation 2 only adds tables,
so CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS per declaration is the whole upgrade; a
store from a newer binary is still refused.

* feat: tally placements from a per-namespace row table

Since #235 every launch counted the cpus other VMs hold by scanning and
fully decoding every VM record in both backend namespaces inside the
serialized write transaction. On the sqlite store with realistic 1.5 KB
records that is 0.93 ms at 100 records, 8.4 ms at 1000 and 16.3 ms at
2000, all under the single writer lock, so a clone burst on a dense
host queues its tallies behind each other.

Each VM namespace gains a placements table, one row per placed VM
holding its cpu-list, mirrored in the one place records are written:
vmTx.Put upserts or deletes the row from the record's queue pins or
cpuset and vmTx.Del drops it. The tally scans those rows. Same bench
after: 0.13 ms at 100, 0.42 ms at 1000, 0.73 ms at 2000, and the bytes
read no longer grow with record size. The json engine declares the
table optional, so legacy files decode unchanged.

A VM placed by the previous binary and still running has no row until
its record is next written; launches right after an upgrade may not
see its pins until then.

* docs: note the schema generation upgrade on open

* review: name the vm transaction func type and fix the busy retry comment

The func type spelled out three times gets a named type (Style Self-Check item 8); the const comment described busyRetryPause under busyRetryCeiling's line.

* meta: refuse an older schema generation and upgrade by script

Open now fails closed in both directions: a store from a newer binary as before, and one stamped behind the binary's generation with the upgrade script named. The upgrade itself moves out of the binary into scripts/meta-upgrade.py, run once after the binary swap: it creates the tables generation 2 declares, writes one placement row for every record that carries a placement (the VMs the previous binary launched and left running, which the launch tally would otherwise not see), and stamps the generation in one transaction under a 5 s busy timeout; on a json root it adds the same rows to each VM namespace file under the engine's flock. Rerunning is a no-op.

InitIfMissing goes back to creating or repairing a store only: nothing one-off belongs in store bootstrap or on the launch path.

* storebench: declare the placements table; pin the row mirror on both engines

The placement mirror in vmTx.Put writes a table storebench never declared, so its sqlite arm failed with a scope error and its json arm silently dropped the rows. The row-follows-record test now runs on the sqlite engine too, where an undeclared table is refused rather than ignored.

* meta-upgrade: ship the script in the release archives and refuse a root without a store

The store's refusal names scripts/meta-upgrade.py, so the release and debug archives now carry it next to the binary (goreleaser's files list replaces the default license and readme set, hence they are listed too). A --root-dir with neither meta.db nor a VM namespace file exits non-zero instead of reporting nothing, so a mistyped root does not read as an upgraded one. The json path writes the upgraded file to its .prev generation as well, the way the engine and the convert tool keep both generations valid, so a later torn main cannot fall back to a file without the rows.

review: sixteen fixes, simplifications, docs aligned with the code (#237)

* fix: propagate CNI provider errors from VM network cleanup

Cleanup swallowed a failed CNI provider init and returned nil, so finishVMTeardown finalized the record, name and tombstone while the netns and IPAM lease were still allocated, with no log line. The init only fails on a broken meta store or an EnsureDirs error, never on a missing conflist, so the swallow protected nothing.

* fix: register every config key with viper so its COCOON_* variable reaches Unmarshal

AutomaticEnv binds only registered keys; use_firecracker, log.filename, log.usejson, socket_wait_timeout_seconds, terminate_grace_period_seconds, metering.backend and metering.file.path were documented as config-file-only for that reason. Registering them with their zero defaults keeps every effective default where the code applies it.

* fix: keep vm state inside the VMState enum on the wire

ReconcileState returned the display string "stopped (stale)", which vm ls -o json and vm inspect serialized into the typed state field. It now returns the state and a stale flag; the table renders the suffix, JSON carries the enum.

* simplify: build the image GC pin sources once per process

pinnedElsewhere rebuilt both hypervisor backends and the snapshot backend inside the recheck closure, which image GC calls once per unreferenced blob under that blob's lock. The construction now happens on the first call; PinnedBlobIDs is still re-read per blob.

* review: trim comments to one fact in cmd/core and cliutil

* fix: tighten CLI argument and flag handling on vm and snapshot commands

vm list and snapshot list rejected nothing, so a stray argument was silently dropped. --bridge and --network are now mutually exclusive on clone as well as create, through cobra, replacing the hand check that only create ran. vm debug defaults --ch to the configured ch_binary, names the cgroup knobs it ignores, and says which devices the printed command omits.

* fix: preflight the snapshot name on import

Import validated only the name's shape and extracted the whole archive before insertRecord rejected a taken name; it now runs the same name-index check save and hibernate use.

* fix: emit the JSON envelope before returning a partial batch or resize error

vm start/stop/rm --output json returned the joined error and no envelope when one VM in the batch failed, so the successes were reported nowhere; clone did the same when the VM was up but its NIC resize failed. The envelope now goes out first and the error still sets the exit status.

* fix: pass the meta engine to the detached reseed child

The child re-execs with the resolved dirs but no config file, so a json root that also holds a meta.db resolved to sqlite, missed the VM and skipped the reseed silently. The parent now exports COCOON_META_BACKEND with the engine it resolved.

* storebench: document every mode and fail on an unwritable profile path

* review: move the log stream constants to their file and trim two comments

* docs: every config key now has an env variable; vm debug --ch defaults to ch_binary

* fix: cgroup GC skips a scope that a concurrent launch populated

The hypervisor snapshot is read before the cgroup one, so a create that lands between them shows up as an unreferenced but populated scope; rmdir then fails with EBUSY and the GC run reported a failure for a VM that is fine. EBUSY is now a skip, which is what the module's never-kills-scope-members promise already meant.

* simplify: drop nil-only returns, dead branches and a redundant poll clamp

daemon.New never failed, so its error return and the caller's handling go; convergeExit compares the transition generation before paying the /proc probe; the poll batch and the ready slice share one constant, removing the min clamp; Cloud Hypervisor's runtime-file arg had an unreachable file mode and the queue affinity encoder handled a multi-cpu list its only producer never builds.

* review: unexport package-local identifiers, name a literal, trim comments

Symbols with no caller outside their package lose the export (cgroup bounds, extend/fs queue defaults, vfio normalizePath, daemon errAlreadyRunning); the fs id prefix joins the const block like its disk and net siblings; restating godocs go and two comments lose a stale seam reference and an issue number.

* fix: Firecracker validates clone data disks before launch, process logs append across launches, a dead console socket is dropped

A clone's --data-disk specs were validated only after the VM had booted, resumed and hot-plugged the drives, so a relative mount path killed a freshly booted clone; the combined set is now checked before launch, as Cloud Hypervisor already did. Both backends truncated the VMM process log on every launch, wiping the crash log a restart was meant to preserve; they now append. A failed console relay left console.sock on disk, which inspect then reported as a console nobody served.

* simplify: share the locked device-op preamble across backends and fold single-use helpers

Both backends opened a device operation with the same client, ops-lock and entry-guard sequence; Backend.LockedRunningOp now carries it, and Cloud Hypervisor resumes an ownerless pause inside lockedDeviceOp instead of at each of three call sites. fcAPI, captureWindow and the package-level PreflightRestore had one caller each and are folded; the plumbing-returned-N guard could not fire, since both Plumbing implementations return exactly one config per spec; startConsoleRelay drops an unused ctx; FinalizeRestore uses errors.Is like its neighbours.

* review: trim hypervisor comments that restate their code

* fix: image backends stamp the VM's image identity only after validation, and four smaller image fixes

ResolveImage probes every backend, so a backend that found the ref but failed a blob check left its type and digest on the VM record while another backend's storage configs were used; the next clone or restore then pulled the wrong image. The erofs version regex now anchors on mkfs.erofs, so a version-bearing line from another tool cannot satisfy the floor the check exists for. The cloudimg convert target is process-unique: two importers of one digest could both pass the convert lock and one renamed the other's half-written file into the blob store. scanBootFiles skipped a kernel or initrd stored with a leading slash, as a plain tar cf writes them. A chunked download no longer reports a negative total; a part that fails to close after the blob is committed is logged, not returned as an import failure.

* simplify: image Ops take normalizers and an EntrySize method instead of two callbacks

Ops.LookupRefs only ever varied by the normalizer list, so Inspect and Delete call LookupOne and LookupRefs directly with Normalizers; Sizer was the same closure in both backends and becomes Entry.EntrySize. finishQcow2Import builds its own logger; an explicit DirOnly: false goes.

* review: trim image comments to one fact and spell a magic prefix as a string literal

* fix: a CNI teardown that resumes another operation's tombstone finishes it and refuses

Acquire hands back any pending tombstone, and teardownProtocol adopted its mode and payload as if they were the caller's: vm rm over an interrupted vm net remove swept only that subset and reported success with the netns and the other NICs still plumbed, while vm net remove over an interrupted vm rm tore down every NIC of a live VM. A resumed tombstone is now finished and the call refused with ErrConflict unless it is the same intent (an aggregate retry, or a subset retry within the interrupted subset), mirroring guardAdd and the hypervisor entry guard.

* fix: CNI GC reports a lock error instead of logging it as busy

A TryLock failure was printed as "vm lock busy" in the collect pass and dropped silently in the recover pass, so a permanent lock-file failure skipped that VM forever without a signal.

* fix: cloud-init enables password auth only when there is a user to hold the password

--user "" passed Validate and rendered ssh_pwauth: true with neither the root nor a user account given a password.

* simplify: drop the unreachable bridge Verify branch and the TAP tuning forwarder, cut the prefix once

Verify's empty-expected branch had no caller: the only one returns early for a bridge VM without NetworkConfigs. TuneTAP had one caller that discarded its error. ifIndex checked the eth prefix twice.

* review: unexport netQueueSize and tombstone resume, rename shadowing locals, trim comments

* fix: validate cocoon's sparse map on extraction, mask extracted modes, clone through the portable ioctl

extractFileSparse trusted the PAX sparse map: a negative length copied nothing silently and a map shorter than the entry left zeros where data belonged, the corruption verifyFromDirCOW already guards on the --from-dir path; the map's segments must now fit the file and sum to the entry size. Extracted files no longer inherit setuid/setgid bits from a user-supplied tar. The FICLONE number was hard-coded for amd64/arm64; unix.IoctlFileClone carries the per-arch value.

* simplify: drop dead expectArg disjuncts, use the unix seek constants and a one-shot time.After

strings.Contains(s, "") is always true, so the empty-expectArg branches never changed a result; seekData/seekHole restate unix.SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE; a stopped one-shot timer buys nothing since Go 1.23.

* review: trim utils comments to one fact; range over the block size in a test

* fix: a closed sqlite store errors instead of panicking

Close nilled the pooled handles outside the mutex, so a View or Update after CloseMetaStore, or a GC pass still running when the daemon closed the store, dereferenced a nil *sql.DB. sql.DB.Close is idempotent and a closed handle returns a real error, so the nils bought nothing.

* simplify: cheaper meta transactions and lookups

Update built a logger and boxed four values on every transaction for a debug line nobody reads; only the slow-transaction warning stays. The reader pool follows GOMAXPROCS, which honours the cgroup CPU limit. Resolve checks existence through GetRaw instead of decoding the whole record twice. The filesystem magics come from x/sys/unix; the flock retry loop drops a branch the pinned gofrs/flock cannot reach; withLocked builds its logger only on the error paths; appendTable is package-local.

* review: name the store transaction callbacks, strip a stale spec stamp and trim meta and lock comments

ViewFunc and UpdateFunc replace the func(Reader) error and func(Writer) error spellings repeated across the interface, both engines and the contract tests; restating godocs go and the rest shrink to one fact.

* fix: snapshot LRU treats a never-accessed record as created, and a failed export removes its partial tree

Records written before v0.5.0 carry a zero LastAccessedAt, which pickLRU read as infinitely old, so the first --snapshot-age run after an upgrade evicted every legacy snapshot; both the pick and the under-lease revalidation now fall back to CreatedAt. ExportToDir left the files it had copied when a copy failed, and the retry then refused the non-empty target forever.

* simplify: snapshot GC stats data dirs after the read transaction closes

* review: trim snapshot and types comments to one fact

* review: drop an enum roster from a config comment, cut a test range once, name the last receiver

* test: reuse the socket server and seed helpers, assert what two tests only skipped or logged

The clone hot-plug test hand-rolled the unix-socket HTTP stub serveCHAPI already wraps; two restore tests inlined the stopped-VM seeding start_test.go provides. TestIsProcessAlive_DeadProcess skipped instead of failing when a reaped pid read as alive, TestVerifyProcessCmdline_WrongBinary asserted nothing and is gone, and TestRestore_CloseWaitsForGoroutine only logged what TestRestore_DoubleCloseNoPanic already covers.

* docs: align every page with the code

Two full reads of the docs against the implementation: launch timeout scope, the stale state row, clone-created data disks never auto-mounting, quarantine after a failed restore, the console escape sequence, Firecracker's single-queue TAPs and MMIO default, image rm leaving blobs to gc, the 20 GiB cap scoped to URL downloads, container images without boot files rejected, clone flags that do not exist, restore-mode behaviour per backend, the post-clone hint order and its DHCP and Windows variants, export --to-dir and the repack warning, digest-pinned --pull, conflist parse failures, required --nics, the 30 s eject timeout, netns lifetime, net_scope changes, device detach semantics per backend, gc phases and summary counts, binary size suffixes, and the fork's fix list stated the same way on every page.

* test: pin the closed sqlite store, leading-slash boot files, the differing-subset teardown refusal and the viper key roster

A closed store used to panic; a plain tar cf stores /boot/vmlinuz with a leading slash; a vm net removal over another removal's tombstone must finish it and refuse, which no test encoded; the viper key list is hand-maintained and has lost keys twice, so the roster is now derived from the config struct's tags. The five tombstone tests share one lease-and-mark helper.

* docs: name the recovery contract of an interrupted network teardown

* docs: correct Windows import and Firecracker capabilities

fix: JSON outputs carry a stale flag; docs name the shipped Windows agent version (#238)

* fix: vm list and inspect JSON carry a stale flag for a running record whose VMM is gone

The enum fix in #237 kept the typed state clean but dropped the only signal a JSON consumer had that a record still reads running while its process is dead; the table kept the (stale) suffix. Both JSON renderers now emit "stale": true next to the reconciled state.

* docs: the Windows images bake cocoon-agent v0.2.3

* cut: image backends resolve one VM's config instead of a batch

Images.Config took a slice of VMs and returned per-VM slices, but its only callers (ResolveImage here, one site in cocoon-macos) wrap a single VM and index [0]; both implementations aborted the whole batch on the first miss, so a multi-VM caller would have had to group by backend first anyway. Single-VM signature, no loop, two fewer allocations per backend probe.

* docs: name JSON VM status commands accurately

* docs: pin the install links to v0.6.6 and give the README the same download step

The release page and the README now name the same versioned archive and the doctor script at the same tag, so a reader lands on the binary the docs describe instead of whatever latest resolves to at read time.

feat: cloudimg exports DownloadBlob behind a Doer, sniffs before writing and reuses the probe reply (#243)

The blob download pipeline was unexported and bound to *http.Client, so cocoon-macos re-derived it against oras's auth.Client. DownloadBlob takes any Do(*http.Request) client and keeps the same algorithm: one GET with an 8-byte Range asks for support; a 206 with a total size sniffs those bytes, then fans the ranges out; a 200 is the whole file and is streamed as is, so a server that ignores Range costs one request instead of two; only a 206 without a total still re-requests. The serial stream peeks its first bytes before the first write, so a URL serving HTML is refused with an empty temp file instead of after a full transfer; the post-download sniff in pull goes. The Range path issues the same requests as before.

Closes #239, closes #137

refactor: types owns the data-disk spec parser, ParseDirectIO and the size floor (#242)

The --data-disk grammar (size=, name=, fstype=, mount=, directio=, the 16 MiB floor) was parsed in cmd/core and floored by a hypervisor constant, so a second consumer of the flag had to copy both rather than import hypervisor and its transitive dependencies. types already owns DataDiskSpec and ValidDataDiskName; the parser and the floor join them, cmd/core keeps the flag-prefixed error and the guest-policy defaults (ext4, dataN, /mnt/<name>).

Closes #240

fix: the event stream carries the stale flag like list and inspect (#244)

* fix: the event stream carries the stale flag like list and inspect

vm status --event -o json reconciles a dead VMM to stopped exactly as list and inspect do, but its envelope still carried the bare record, so the one JSON path that watches for changes could not tell a crash-reconciled stop from a clean one. The envelope now wraps the same vmOutput, so all three JSON renderers share one shape.

* docs: vm status takes --format, not -o

fix: size flags accept the Kubernetes Gi spelling (#246)

--memory, --storage, --data-disk size= and gc --snapshot-size each handed their value straight to go-units, which reads 20G and 20GiB but rejects 20Gi, so a Kubernetes-shaped quantity failed on cocoon while cocoon-macos carried its own normaliser. types.ParseSize is the one rule for the family: trim, append B to a trailing i, then go-units; every unit stays binary.

review and refactor (#248)

* fix: InitIfMissing waits out a racing bootstrap instead of failing busy

The pre-lock fast path returned whatever initNeeded said, so a racer that
caught the winner mid-init (file present, WAL switch in flight) surfaced a
transient SQLITE_BUSY as the bootstrap's final answer. A busy or partial
pre-lock answer now falls into the transient flock and the locked recheck
decides; the steady-state path (store present and initialized) still takes
no lock.

* test: RemoveMatching failure test asserts the error it sets up

The test built a read-only directory and then discarded RemoveMatching's
result. It now expects the one removal error and the surviving directory,
and skips under root, where the chmod does not block the removal.

* fix: snapshot import refuses a COW a third-party tar shortened

--from-dir already compared cow.raw against the envelope's storage size,
but the tar import registered the same shortened disk and the clone booted
it. The size gate now lives in the snapshot package and runs on both
paths; the COW file name moves to types so the snapshot store can name it
without importing the hypervisor layer.

* fix: Cloud Hypervisor refuses a hot-attached capture before pausing

The refusal lived in the sidecar builder, so a VM with a hot-attached
disk, vhost-user-fs share or VFIO device paid the whole pause window and a
full vm.snapshot before the capture was discarded; Firecracker already
checks before its pause. The pause hook now reads vm.info and refuses
first; the sidecar check stays as the backstop.

* fix: vm stop refuses a creating placeholder instead of marking it stopped

An ownerless creating record (its create or clone died mid-flight) was
flipped to stopped by vm stop, which removes it from every stale-create
reclaim (reconcile-stale-create, gc, the daemon) while it keeps its name
and half-built run dir. Stop now refuses it the way start does; vm rm
--force on such a record terminates the orphan VMM the way the reclaim
does instead of routing through stop.

* fix: Firecracker restore refuses a snapshot recorded on another VM's drives

Firecracker reopens the drive paths embedded in the vmstate, and restore
sends no override, so vm restore --from-dir --force with an export taken
from another VM on the same host booted the target on the source VM's
live cow.raw and data disks: two VMMs writing one ext4. Cloud Hypervisor
patches config.json with the record's own paths and is unaffected. The
FC preflight now requires every snapshot-resident sidecar path to equal
the target record's path for that slot; shared layers stay exempt.

* fix: CNI network info takes the gateway from the default route when ips[] has none

A conflist whose IPAM advertises the gateway only as a routes[] entry
(static IPAM with a routes list, and other spec-conformant plugins) left
Network.Gateway empty, so the direct-boot ip= line and the cloudimg
netplan gave the guest an address with no default route. The bundled
bridge + host-local config populates ips[].gateway, which hid it.

* fix: stale-running reconcile clears the dead PID with the runtime paths

vm list -o json, vm inspect and vm status --event reported
state=stopped, stale=true and the exited VMM's pid side by side; the
PID now goes with the socket paths.

* test: FindVMMByCmdline tolerates the shell's pre-exec child; FC prefix fixture drops pci=off

Under a dash /bin/sh the forked-not-yet-execed child transiently carries
the parent's cmdline, so the scan can see two pids; the product path
takes the lowest and re-verifies, so the test asserts membership. The
BuildBaseCmdline fixture still carried pci=off, which the FC cmdline has
not contained since --pci landed and create_test pins as absent.

* docs: reconcile pages with the round's fixes and the code as read

snapshots/known-issues: import refuses a shortened COW too; FC restore
reopens recorded paths and refuses another VM's; snapshot lease files
are never reclaimed. devices/known-issues: the hot-attached refusal now
lands before the pause on both backends. vm: creating is refused by
start/stop and reclaimed by the stale-create paths; error is not sticky
once the VM was up; preflight checks presence not size; fsnotify watches
the store's directory. daemon: the creating placeholder is unstamped and
MODIFIED can repeat a generation. gc: locks/vm is normally empty. cli:
vm status is one-shot by default; meta backup leaves DEST.lock.
firecracker: hot-plug runs ahead of the published swagger. networking:
the gateway falls back to the default route. markTransition godoc
narrowed to match.

* fix: deleting a creating placeholder emits no storage.stop

A placeholder never reached FinalizeCreate, so no vm.storage.start
exists for it; vm rm (and rm --force on a live orphan) emitted an
unmatched vm.storage.stop that the ledger's start/stop pairing by id
cannot place, while reconcile-stale-create, gc and the daemon emit
nothing for the same record. Delete now emits only for a record that
finalized.

* docs: name the ValidateResidentPaths precondition

* docs: align networking and restore guidance with current behavior

* fix: recheck VM ownership before network garbage collection

* fix: reject cross-image restores before mutating the VM

* fix: preserve import sources when cached blobs are collected

* fix: bridge gc keeps collecting past one owner lookup failure

One failed owner lookup returned from Collect and left every remaining
orphan TAP for the next pass, while the cni collector reports the same
failure and carries on. The bridge collector now does the same: the
failure is joined into the module's error and the other candidates are
still checked and deleted.

* fix: cgroup gc rechecks VM ownership before removing a scope

The cgroup collector still deleted from the stale snapshot: between
cgroup.Prepare and Cmd.Start a launch's scope exists and is empty, so a
concurrent sweep removed it and the launch failed at CLONE_INTO_CGROUP.
The EBUSY guard only covers a scope that already has a member. The
module now takes the same VMInUse the network collectors got and skips
a scope whose VM record exists, which create writes before Prepare.
The cmd/core test case that asserted ErrAmbiguous is renamed: Inspect
never returns that sentinel (it is cmd/core's cross-backend marker), so
the case only ever covered an unknown read error.

* docs: gc ownership rechecks cover cgroup scopes and rest on record-before-provision

* fix: restore compares image digests only when both sides carry one

The per-side cmp.Or turned a digestless side into a ref-against-digest
comparison that can never match, so an export from a VM record written
before ImageDigest existed (2026-04-23) was refused with --force into a
newer VM of the same base image. Digests are compared when both sides
have one; otherwise the refs are, as they were before digests existed.

* fix: commit republishes a blob collected after its entry check

A pull or import whose blob existed when commit started skipped the
tmp-blob preparation; if GC collected that blob before the blob lock,
commit returned errBlobCacheMiss although the caller's own temp still
held the bytes, so image pull failed after a successful download and
only the next command converged. With a real source in hand commit now
prepares the tmp blob under the lock and publishes it; the cache-miss
error is left for the cache-hit path that has no source to fall back to.

fix: collect a netns entry whose bind mount is already gone (#252)

netns.DeleteNamed returns as soon as unmount fails, so it never unlinks; the
1s WaitFor around it also discarded the error. When the bind mount is already
detached but the file remains, unmount keeps returning EINVAL, the entry
leaks, and every cocoon gc reports a bare timeout for it and exits non-zero.
Treat EINVAL as already-unmounted and unlink the entry, and surface the last
syscall error instead of a naked deadline. Seen on cocoon-test2 during the
2026-09-22 regression: six such entries, each failing every gc run; the new
test reproduces it as root and fails on the parent commit.

Close the exit-detection and snapshot-lease convergence gaps (#253)

* test: gate the netns collection test on CAP_SYS_ADMIN, not euid

root inside an unprivileged container passes the euid check but umount2 returns EPERM, so the test burned the full retry window and failed instead of skipping.

* fix: reap the VMM inside LaunchVMProcess so a dead one fails fast

The socket wait checks liveness with kill(0), and the backends' reaper started only after LaunchVMProcess returned, so a VMM that exited on bad args stayed an unreaped zombie and every failed start paid the full socket timeout. Closes #250.

* fix: wait for a VMM exit through a pidfd instead of a 500ms poll

GracefulStop polled kill(0) every 500ms, so a guest that shut down early still paid up to half a second per stop while the force path and the daemon watcher already waited on the kernel.

* fix: reclaim snapshot lease files instead of leaking one per snapshot

Snapshot leases used gofrs/flock directly and nothing ever unlinked them, so every snapshot ever created left a zero-byte file in a directory whose purpose is to be reclaimable. Moving the shared lease onto lock/flock lets the exclusive side be transient: release unlinks under the inode re-verification that keeps a waiting reader from splitting exclusion, and GC sweeps the backlog. Closes #249.

* review: lint the test sources and drop the dead nolint directives

run.tests was false, so 22k lines of test code never met a linter and the _test.go exclusion rules below it were dead config. Enabling it surfaced an append onto a package-level magic slice, an unclosed response body, and five stale idioms. nolintlint joins the set and the 87 no-op directives it and the missing mnd linter left behind are gone; shadow and dogsled are excluded for tests, where each err is consumed at its own declaration and a four-value call legitimately drops three.

* fix: reclaim only a transient lock file that exists

gofrs TryLock opens with O_CREATE, so ReclaimTransient on an already-gone path created the file, unlinked it again and reported a reclaim. Both sweepers log "collected ... reason=orphan-lease" on that true, so the VM lock GC could announce a collection it invented; the snapshot sweep carried its own stat guard, which now belongs to the primitive.

* cut: the VM lock GC scans through utils.ScanFileStems

The sibling snapshot sweep already reads its lease directory that way; this one hand-rolled ReadDir, the suffix walk and the ErrNotExist collapse that scanDir performs, and with them four imports.

* review: drop the reapProcess godoc that restates its call site

The call site above reapProcess already carries the zombie constraint, and the signature carries the rest.

* cut: fold the GC reason loops, the pipe-reader constructor and the double TAP lookup

Three single-use shapes the round surfaced: BuildGCModule wrote the same first-wins assignment three times, NewPipeStreamReader was an exported constructor with one caller in its own file and no consumer anywhere in the workspace, and CleanupTAPs probed every TAP with LinkByName only to have tearDownTAPs look it up again. Import also re-implemented the --name/--description contract that SnapshotNameFlags owns for Save and Hibernate, and listAndFilter sorted before filtering where its sibling statusOnce filters first.

* fix: refreshVM logs under its own name, not the reseed verb

finishClone calls it on the clone path, so a failed inspect during vm clone logged cmd.vm.reseed and said "before reseed" for a verb the operator never ran.

* fix: a failed stop keeps the placement of a VMM that is still alive

markTransition cleared CPUSet and QueueCPUs on every non-Running transition, so HandleStopResult's error path, the one path that has just proved the VMM alive, deleted the VM's placement row while the cgroup scope kept the pin. The next --cpuset-cpus auto launch then double-booked those cpus, and nothing restored the row: ReconcileToRunning only clears, the supervisor bails at confirmDead, and the cgroup GC protects a scope whose VM still inspects. Only Stopped proves the VMM gone; Error keeps the claim until the next start re-places it or rm deletes it. Origin 0ac19dcf (#235).

* fix: the export envelope lists its files so a truncated import fails instead of registering

archive/tar returns the same io.EOF for a proper end-of-archive and for a stream cut exactly at an entry boundary, so ExtractTar accepted a snapshot export missing whole files and import registered it as healthy; only vm clone or restore later noticed, with no pointer to the short transfer. The gzip path already verified its trailer, plain tar had nothing. Export now writes the data dir's file list into snapshot.json and import checks every listed file landed; envelopes without the list import as before. VerifyCOWSize cannot carry this: a cloudimg snapshot legitimately has no cow.raw. Origin 1da5c29b.

* perf: walk /proc once per start batch and read the cpu topology once per process

Every vm start walked /proc in full for its liveness check (about 3 syscalls per host process, 4.5k on a 384-thread node) and DeleteAll had hoisted one scan for exactly that but only used it for the orphan kill, leaving its own liveness check on the per-VM walk. StartAll now scans once like DeleteAll and both hand the scan down. Every launch also re-read the cache-domain sysfs tree (about 38 files, 541us at 384 cpus in a fixture) and Place read thread_siblings_list inside the single-writer transaction; the topology is memoized per Backend with cores precomputed, so the serialized section is arithmetic, and HostCPUCount reads /online once.

* fix: re-verify a batch /proc scan hit under the ops lock before trusting it

vm start scans /proc before it takes a VM's ops lock. A start queued behind a stop of the same VM saw the VMM in that scan, found the pidfile gone once the stop released the lock, took the stale hit as a live VMM, flipped the record to Running with a compute.start, and exited 0 with nothing running; vm rm had the same stale check and refused a stopped VM without --force.

A cached hit now counts only if its cmdline still matches. Cost: zero on a miss, one /proc/<pid>/cmdline read per hit, and a hit is only consulted after the pidfile check failed. Regression from 811870e (#253).

Both empty paths printed the human line to stdout even in JSON mode, so a machine consumer had to sniff for '[' (sandboxd's engine does). vm list already prints [] in the same case; table output is unchanged.

Since the script reads cocoon vm inspect, a dead running VM arrives already reconciled to stopped with pid 0 and "stale": true, so the running-but-dead FAIL never fired; it now keys on .stale. * fix: snapshot export fails when closing the written archive fails

The deferred close discarded its error, so a filesystem that reports a deferred write error only at close (NFS, FUSE) left a short archive while the command exited 0. The close error now joins the return value and takes the existing remove-on-error path.

* fix: vm debug --fc warns about the Cloud Hypervisor-only flags it ignores

The Firecracker branch returned before --max-cpu, --balloon, --cow and --ch were read, so --cow X silently printed cow-<name>.raw; debug already warns for every other flag it drops.

detachReseed and signalReseed tag their own names: they run on the clone and restore paths, never under vm reseed. initNeeded/failedInit take the caller's ctx and query with QueryRowContext. open's synchronous parameter no longer shadows the sync import. importQcow2Concat drops a named result nothing reads. Layout only (/code File Organization: utilities grouped by functionality, not interleaved): tarFileFrom, whose only caller is rewindAndTarFull, moves out of the extract helpers to sit below it.

Wrong: launchCloneFn is handed lease files, not drive FDs; reader handles do prepare scan; os.ReadDir sorts by name. NetNumQueues and VMIDPrefix use max/min, procStartTime uses strings.CutLast, vmIPs falls back with cmp.Or, and the LRU candidates append through slices.AppendSeq. * review: one owner for the command-group contract

Every verb group took Args: cobra.NoArgs plus RunE: cliutil.ShowHelp so a mistyped verb fails instead of printing help and exiting 0 (#259). The pair was spelled out at seven sites with no test, so the next group would drop it silently. cliutil.GroupCommand owns it; ShowHelp stays exported for cocoon-macos. TestCommandGroupsRejectAnUnknownVerb runs every group bare (help, nil) and with a bogus verb (unknown command), and fails if GroupCommand loses NoArgs.

* cut: vestigial error paths, single-caller wrappers and a dead field

- Topology.Place has not failed since #253 moved the sysfs reads into ReadTopology; its error result and placement's unreachable check go.
- pinResolvedBlobs repeated images.PinBlobs' empty-set guard; the launch path calls owner.PinBlobs.
- ExportToDir hand-rolled utils.ListRegularFiles.
- PipeStream's Close/CloseWithError branch: CloseWithError(nil) is Close.
- The FC failed-relay goroutine moves into the switch arm that is the only way relayErr can be non-nil.

- isBusy restated mapErr's BUSY/LOCKED mapping; the busy loop now tests the mapped error. The non-busy path returns the same mapErr result, and the retry-ceiling error never carried err.

* cut: BuildIPParams joins the first two DNS servers instead of hand-building them

dns0/dns1 and the nested param appends spelled out strings.Join over at most two entries. Every caller's list comes from config.DNSServers, which drops blank entries, so the joined form is byte-identical. TestBuildIPParams pins 0, 1, 2 and 3 servers plus a skipped NIC; it was written against the old code and passes unchanged.

* cut: retire the image-ref normalizer that never matched

normalizeRef promised to expand "ubuntu:24.04" to docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 but returned name.ParseReference(s).String(), which is s itself for both tags and digests (go-containerregistry keeps the original string), and fetchImage keys the index by that same string. The normalizer lookup in LookupRefs therefore re-ran the exact-key miss it followed. normalizeRef, Ops.Normalizers, the variadic normalizers parameter and the OCI wiring go; no caller in the workspace passed another normalizer.

* cut: sweepLeases trusts the lease lock, not the data dir listing

sweepLeases also spared every lease whose id still had a data dir, but that never kept a lease alive that mattered. A build or reader that holds the lease makes ReclaimTransient report busy. An orphan dir's unheld lease is taken exclusively by Collect in the same pass and unlinked on release. Nothing reopens a crashed Import's random id, a crashed Create keeps its lease through the pending record, and every acquirer re-verifies the inode it locked, so unlinking an unheld lease file loses no state. The records alone now decide which leases stay.

TestGCKeepsALeaseHeldByALiveBuild is unchanged. TestGCCollectsACrashedBuildAndItsLeaseInOnePass pins the crashed-build case: the orphan dir and its lease both go in one pass. Round 2026-09-25: CLI argument checks, console signal, CNI/bridge recovery and teardown, cloud-init online gating (#268)

* cli: every zero-argument command rejects positional arguments

gc, image list, meta init, meta convert, version and daemon had no Args, so cobra accepted and ignored stray positionals: 'cocoon gc --snapshot 720h' left 720h as an ignored positional and ran an unfiltered snapshot eviction, and 'cocoon meta convert json' converted to the configured backend, not to json. A command-tree test now fails for any runnable leaf whose Use names no argument yet accepts one.

* vm console: close the console connection when the signal context ends

The root command traps SIGINT/SIGTERM, so a signal cancelled ctx but left Relay blocked on the connection; on Firecracker the single-session relay stayed occupied.

* cni: record a recovered NIC that has no network record

A vm net shrink killed between plumbing.Remove and the VM record truncate leaves a NIC config with no network record. Recovery re-added the NIC but never wrote a record, so rm and gc never released its IPAM lease and quiesce skipped it. Stage an intent for such a NIC before ADD, like a fresh one, so a crash mid-recovery also stays reclaimable.

* cni: treat a netns entry that is not a mounted netns as absent

A kill between unmount and unlink in netns.DeleteNamed, or a bind mount that failed after the O_EXCL create, leaves a plain file under /var/run/netns. ensureNetns only stat'ed it, so recovery never recreated the netns, and teardown handed the path to plugin DEL, which rejects a non-netns path, so the netns removal and sweep never ran. Recreate such an entry in ensureNetns, and run DEL without a netns path (optional for DEL per the CNI spec) when the netns is gone.

* bridge: verify each TAP is attached to the bridge

A kill between CreateTAP and attachBridgeUp leaves a persistent TAP off the bridge; Verify only checked that it exists, so every later start skipped recovery and booted without connectivity. Recovery re-attaches the existing TAP.

* metadata: render RequiredForOnline in the [Link] section

systemd.network only accepts RequiredForOnline= under [Link]; under [Network] networkd ignored it, so a silent secondary DHCP NIC held systemd-networkd-wait-online until its timeout.

* review: correct comments that contradict the code

Comment rule: a comment states what the code does. Firecracker Delete blocks on the ops lock while a clone holds the shared lease; the terminate grace period applies to every VMM; a recovery re-add re-attaches an existing TAP since TUNSETIFF runs without IFF_TUN_EXCL.

* review: apply the comment case register

Comment register rule: an own-line comment starts uppercase, a trailing same-line comment starts lowercase.

* review: tag method loggers as pkg.Method

Logging rule: 62 of 65 method loggers tag pkg.Method without the receiver type (cni.Add, meta.sqlite.Update, daemon.Run); align the three that carried it.

* review: sequence the concurrent backup test with synctest

Test rule: timing-dependent concurrency tests use testing/synctest, not real sleeps. synctest.Wait returns once the second Backup is parked on the destination lock, replacing a 150ms sleep; with the lock removed the test fails 10 of 10 runs.

* metadata: only the primary NIC gates network-online in the netplan config

On a fresh cloudimg VM cloud-init renders network-config through netplan, and netplan's 10-netplan-idN.network files win over the 15-cocoon fallback files, so a secondary DHCP NIC with no lease held systemd-networkd-wait-online for its full 2 min timeout on every boot. Measured on Ubuntu 22.04 with a DHCP server that answers only NIC0: cloud-init finished at Up 173 s, after 'Failed to start Wait for Network to be Configured'. Secondary NICs are now optional: true, matching the RequiredForOnline=no the fallback files already carry.

* cni: fail Verify while a network teardown is pending

A vm net shrink killed after Remove committed its deleting tombstone but
before the TAP delete and the record truncate leaves the record with the
removed NIC and a pending tombstone. The next vm start passed Verify (the
TAP still carried its redirect), the VMM attached that NIC, and the next
gc rolled the tombstone forward under the running guest: it released the
lease and deleted the TAP, since a running VM does not hold the VM lock.
vk-cocoon runs vm net under exec.CommandContext, so its shutdown SIGKILLs
an in-flight resize.

Verify now fails while a tombstone is pending, so the start takes the
Prepare+Add recovery path. guardAdd rolls the teardown forward and answers
ErrConflict; the recovery retries its Add once, which rebuilds the NIC
from its persisted MAC/IP, so the start converges in one attempt instead
of failing (vk-cocoon evicts a pod whose VM restart fails). A retry that
still conflicts fails the start as before. The start path pays one
networks-namespace read per CNI start.

* hypervisor: persist the network a NIC grow resolves

A VM created with --nics 0 never runs Add at create time, so its record
keeps Config.Network empty, and netResizeAdd persisted only the new
NetworkConfigs although Add resolved the conflist into rec.Config.
Recovery and later grows then re-resolved the empty name to whatever
conflist sorts first at that moment, while teardown used the NIC record's
own type: once an operator added a conflist that sorts first, recovery
re-added the NIC on the new network with its old IP (host-local rejects
it, so every start fails) or leaked a lease no teardown releases.

appendNetworkConfig now records the resolved network in the same write
when the record has none, and never overwrites a recorded one.

* cni: fail recovery closed when the pre-recovery DEL fails

The recovery path released each NIC's old plumbing with a CNI DEL before
re-adding it, but warned and continued when that DEL failed, while the
fresh path fails closed on a failed reclaim (88dcf95): a strict IPAM
plugin then fails the ADD and buries the root cause, and a lenient one
double-allocates.

nicRuntime becomes prepareNICRuntime and returns the DEL failure, so the
recovery fails with it and never ADDs over an unreleased lease. The NIC
is counted as attempted before the DEL, so the rollback retries the DEL
and a staged intent row is dropped only after a DEL succeeds.

* review: correct cni comments and messages that contradict the code

The Add rollback said a kept intent record waits for GC, but GC never
collects an active VM's records; a later re-add, vm rm or GC releases it,
so the log lines now only say the record is kept. Remove's duplicate-record
comment rested on a failed reclaim leaving duplicates, which 88dcf95 made
impossible by failing the Add closed; the comment goes. deleteNetns wrapped
its timeout without verb-noun text.

* review: derive the cni test codec from production and order its helpers

The test codec re-declared the table layout JSONNamespace already owns;
it now derives from it, so the two cannot drift. recordingExec and its
methods moved above the utility funcs (utilities below a type's methods).

The known issue scoped the ip= limitation to a cold boot after a stop, but the first vm run of an ubuntu:24.04 OCI VM with --nics 2 also comes up with eth0 unconfigured (only the last ip= reaches /run/net-*.conf), and the only listed workaround covered clones.

fix(cmd): image list prints [] under --format json on an empty store (#270)

The empty-store sentence went to every format, so a caller parsing the JSON list of a fresh node failed on "No images found." until the first image landed; sandboxd's image check logged that every minute.

boot: hand arm64 OCI kernels to EDK2 over fw_cfg (#271)

On arm64 a direct-kernel-booted guest only sees a device tree, so it
never gets ACPI: vm net and device removal return success while the
guest notices neither, and the ejected NIC's tap leaks on every clone.
Cloud Hypervisor upstream now boots a kernel through EDK2 when
--firmware and --kernel are given together with --fw-cfg-config
(cloud-hypervisor/cloud-hypervisor#8910); EDK2 pulls the kernel,
initramfs and command line over fw_cfg and starts them through its EFI
stub, and the guest gets ACPI, PCI hotplug and an rtc-efi clock. The
fork's own arm64 ACPI patch is retired in favour of that path.

On arm64, OCI images now carry the node firmware next to the kernel and
the Cloud Hypervisor payload adds --firmware and
--fw-cfg-config kernel=on,cmdline=on,initramfs=on,acpi_table=on; every
component is named because with --firmware the VMM no longer loads the
initramfs itself. x86_64 boots are unchanged, as are Firecracker and
records created by older cocoons. cocoon-check installs the EDK2
CLOUDHV_EFI.fd build ch-97eeb7b09 as the aarch64 firmware, verified
against a pinned digest, and flags a firmware or a cloud-hypervisor
build that cannot take this path.

Verified on a c4a-highmem-96-metal node with the same flags injected by
a wrapper: Android 16 and Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 OCI images boot with EFI,
ACPI and a correct pre-NTP clock, hotplug works, clones get their own
MAC and lease with no tap left behind, and cold boot costs 0.16-0.19 s
more.

fix(cmd): image list encodes an empty store as [] under --format json (#272)

#270 stopped printing the empty-store sentence for JSON but still handed the
encoder a nil slice, so a fresh node printed null. Go callers decode null into
an empty slice; jq and Python iteration fail on it. The empty case now
mirrors snapshot list: an explicit empty array for JSON, the sentence
otherwise. Found by the 2026-09-28 two-host E2E.
